title: MedMCP: An Open Agentic Ecosystem for Medical Imaging Workflows
abstract: Deep learning has driven rapid progress in medical image analysis, with methods for tasks such as organ segmentation, anomaly detection, and radiology report generation now matching or surpassing expert performance on several benchmarks. While many methods are released as open source, their routine adoption by clinicians and medical researchers remains limited. The bottleneck is not a lack of capable tools, but the absence of infrastructure to make them accessible to non-technical users. To break this barrier, we present MedMCP , an agentic framework that solves this last-mile problem along two axes: (1) a local agentic workspace that lets users apply state-of-the-art image analysis methods through natural language, and (2) a community-driven tool ecosystem that lets developers deploy and distribute capabilities as validated, independently testable servers. MedMCP enforces a strict orchestration-execution boundary in which a local language model translates user intent into workflow plans, while all image analysis is delegated to domain-specific tools. The framework runs entirely on-premise, every side-effecting operation passes through a human-in-the-loop permission gate, and a full provenance trail links each output to the tools, parameters, and inputs that produced it. An inspectable workspace lets users verify intermediate results rather than blindly trusting the agent, and completed sessions distill into deterministic, shareable workflows that re-execute without the agent, turning one-off interactions into reproducible analyses. This paper introduces the project’s general idea and describes the design principles that guide its development. Beyond a single toolkit, we envision MedMCP as a community-driven platform where each contributed tool becomes easily accessible, compounding individual efforts into shared capability. https://medmcp.ai https://github.com/medmcp

title: Longitudinal changes in motor network activity and connectivity in patients with suspected Transcient Ischemic Attack: an exploratory fMRI study
abstract: Background and Objectives Transient ischemic attack (TIA) diagnosis is challenging because it relies mainly on clinical assessment and exclusion of common differential. Functional MRI (fMRI) may provide a diagnostic biomarker by detecting transient brain dysfunction not visible on conventional imaging. This pilot study aimed to characterize acute motor-task BOLD activation in patients with suspected DWI-negative TIA and compare functional patterns between confirmed TIA and alternative diagnoses. Secondary objectives were to assess longitudinal changes in activation and connectivity at 3 months. Methods In this prospective single-center study, adults presenting within 24 h of transient anterior-circulation neurological symptoms underwent conventional MRI and additional motor-task fMRI. Patients with acute DWI lesions were excluded. Final diagnosis was established after 3-month follow-up. Whole-brain analyses, individualized motor cortex region-of-interest (ROI) analyses, and generalized psychophysiological interaction (gPPI) connectivity analyses were performed during the acute phase and at 3 months. Results Eight patients were enrolled; six had complete longitudinal imaging data and were included in the final analyses. Final diagnoses were TIA (n=2), migraine aura (n=2), functional neurological disorder (n=1), and hypoglycemia (n=1). Whole-brain and ROI analyses showed reduced bilateral motor-related BOLD responses during the acute phase in both TIA patients and in the patient with hypoglycemia. In contrast, patients with migraine and functional neurological disorder exhibited less marked longitudinal changes. In TIA patients, motor cortex activation increased at 3 months, tending to normalize toward values observed in non-TIA participants. Connectivity analyses revealed heterogeneous patterns, but the 2 TIA patients demonstrated increased longitudinal connectivity between the motor cortex contralateral to symptoms and other sensorimotor regions, including supplementary motor, premotor, parietal, and postcentral cortices. Discussion These preliminary findings suggest that TIA may be associated with transient bilateral reductions in motor-network activity. Functional abnormalities appeared to improve over time, supporting the hypothesis of reversible network dysfunction. Although limited by the very small sample size, this study provides the first longitudinal assessment of emergency task-based fMRI in rigorously defined TIA and supports further investigation of acute functional MRI as a potential biomarker of transient cerebral dysfunction.

title: CytoRipple: Mapping Tissue Polarization through Subcellular Cytoskeleton Dynamics
abstract: Spatial multi-omic technologies entail simultaneous measurement of tens-to-thousands of molecular features (e.g. RNA, protein). While cell type and state profiling is the major focus of spatial multi-omic analyses, cytoskeletal proteins are often solely utilized for cell segmentation and quality control. Here, we introduce a new computational framework, CytoRipple, that leverages these concomitant spatially-resolved single-cell measurements of cytoskeleton proteins to identify tissue-level vector fields. Polarization vectors are known to associate with cell movement and phenotype, inferring their physical orientation. We validate these associations across biological contexts and reveal how polarization vector fields can be harnessed to discover multi-cellular structures (e.g. “streams” of cells with similar polarizations). These multi-cellular cytoskeleton dynamics associate with distinct phenomena, such as vector “divergence” with CD8 + T cell activation and “streams” with spatially segmented stages of the anti-tumor immune response. Together, these data support a role for CytoRipple in revealing a dynamic layer across spatial multi-omic platforms.

title: Longitudinal associations between neuropsychiatric symptoms, structural and perfusion MRI changes in older adults with Mild Cognitive Impairment
abstract: Neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPS) are highly prevalent in Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), conceptualized as an intermediate clinical state between normal aging and dementia. Although neuroimaging studies have reported associations between NPS and brain alterations in MCI, longitudinal evidence on NPS and their relationship with multimodal MRI measures remains limited. We aimed to investigate (1) longitudinal changes in NPS, volumetric assessment and measurement of regional cerebral blood flow (CBF) within the medial temporal lobe (MTL); (2) associations between longitudinal changes in MRI measures and NPS; (3) whether baseline MRI measures predicted longitudinal changes in NPS. Thirty individuals with MCI aged over 65 years were recruited, of whom eighteen followed up for a mean period of 29 ± 8.9 months. There were significant reductions in total grey matter and white matter volumes, together with volume loss in the bilateral hippocampus, bilateral parahippocampal gyrus and right entorhinal cortex (p FDR< 0.05) over the follow up period. Volume loss in the right parahippocampal gyrus was associated with increase in aggression (p FDR <0.01), and CBF increase in the right hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus was associated with worsening in agitation (p FDR <0.01). Furthermore, lower baseline volume of the right entorhinal cortex was associated with increase in aggression, and lower baseline CBF in the right hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus was associated with worsening of agitation (p FDR <0.05). Our findings highlight the importance of identifying NPS in individuals with MCI and the role of structural and perfusion MRI measures as promising biomarkers for monitoring disease progression and improving risk prediction of conversion to dementia.

title: Vascular Proximity Coverage: A Novel CT-Based Marker of Pulmonary Vascular Distance to the Lung Parenchyma
abstract: RationaleConventional CT-derived pulmonary vascular metrics quantify vascular pruning but do not assess spatial heterogeneity of vascular architecture. In COPD, peripheral microvascular pruning coexists with compensatory central vessel dilation, paradoxically preserving total vessel volume while reducing effective vascular penetration into lung parenchyma. ObjectivesTo develop and validate Vascular Proximity Coverage (VPC), a novel distance-based CT biomarker quantifying spatial efficiency of pulmonary vascular distribution. MethodsThis retrospective analysis included 7,881 COPDGene participants with complete vascular segmentations. VPC is estimated by integrating the area under the cumulative lung tissue coverage curve at distances 0-10 mm from segmented vessel voxels. Multivariable models were used to assess associations with lung function, six-minute walk distance (6MWD), St. Georges Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ), mMRC dyspnea score and all-cause mortality adjusting for demographics, smoking, emphysema, scanner type, and BV5. We stratified the cohort into four groups defined by the median values of BV5 and VPC, yielding discordant (high-BV5/low-VPC, low-BV5/high-VPC) and concordant (high/high, low/low) vascular phenotypes. ResultsVPC declined across disease severity (5.82 {+/-} 0.50 in non-smokers to 5.21 {+/-} 0.64 in GOLD 4; p<0.001). Among spirometrically normal smokers, current smokers showed reduced VPC versus former smokers (5.31 vs. 5.68; p<0.001). Each standard deviation (SD) decrease in VPC was independently associated with reduced 6MWD ({beta}=-16.8 m, 95% CI: -19.5 to -14.0), worse SGRQ ({beta}=1.9, 95% CI: 1.4 to 2.4), and increased dyspnea (RR=1.05, 95% CI: 1.03-1.08; all p<0.001). The lowest VPC quartile, as compared to the reference quartile, was associated with 38% higher mortality (HR=1.38, 95% CI: 1.18-1.62; p<0.001). Based on median thresholds, high-BV5/low-VPC phenotype, compared to High-BV5/High-VPC, showed 24% increased mortality (HR=1.24, 95% CI: 1.08-1.42; p=0.002) despite preserved vessel volume. ConclusionsVPC captures spatial heterogeneity of vascular architecture independent of vessel volume and detects subclinical vascular dysfunction in smokers without airflow obstruction. AT A GLANCE COMMENTARYO_ST_ABSScientific Knowledge on the SubjectC_ST_ABSCurrent CT-based pulmonary vascular metrics, including volume of blood vessels less than 5 mm{superscript 2} cross-sectional area (BV5) and total vessel volume, quantify the amount of visible vasculature but do not assess how effectively vessels reach the lung parenchyma for efficient gas exchange. In COPD, peripheral microvascular pruning commonly coexists with compensatory central vessel dilation, leading to preserved or increased total vascular volume despite compromised functional vascular distribution. What This Study Adds to the FieldVascular Proximity Coverage (VPC) is a novel distance-based CT biomarker that quantifies the spatial efficiency of pulmonary vascular distribution by measuring cumulative lung tissue coverage across distances from vessel walls. In 7,881 COPDGene participants, including non-smokers and PRISm subjects, lower VPC was independently associated with decreased lung function, reduced exercise capacity, worsened quality of life, and increased all-cause mortality over a median 10.8-year follow-up after adjusting for BV5 and emphysema. VPC identified a high-risk phenotype with preserved vessel volume but impaired distribution (high-BV5/low-VPC) that carried 24% increased mortality risk and detected subclinical vascular dysfunction in smokers with normal spirometry.

title: Beyond Agrammatism: Syntax Processing in Chinese Primary Progressive Aphasia
abstract: Syntax processing impairment is a defining feature of primary progressive aphasia (PPA), particularly in the nonfluent/agrammatic variant. However, current models are derived largely from Indo-European languages, and it remains unclear whether the cognitive and neuroanatomical mechanisms of syntax processing generalize to Chinese, an analytic, pro-drop language that encodes grammatical relationships primarily through word order and function words rather than inflectional morphology. Participants were recruited from the international Chinese Language Assessment in PPA cohort and included 64 individuals with PPA (19 logopenic, 15 nonfluent/agrammatic, 15 semantic, and 15 unclassifiable/mixed) and 60 cognitively healthy controls. Participants completed sentence comprehension and production tasks with systematically manipulated syntactic features. Item-level linguistic determinants were examined using ridge regression, diagnostic performance using receiver operating characteristic analyses, and neuroanatomical correlates using voxel-based morphometry of structural MRI. Performance on sentence comprehension and production was influenced by grammatical and lexical features. Subject-relative clauses, passive constructions, a higher proportion of function words, longer character length, and greater lexical content were associated with poorer performance among participants with PPA. Sentence comprehension was impaired in the logopenic, nonfluent/agrammatic, and semantic variants, even when isolated to the syntactic component of the sentence comprehension task. Similarly, sentence production was impaired across all PPA variants (all P < 0.01 versus controls). No significant differences were observed among PPA variants. Adjusted receiver operating characteristic analyses demonstrated high discrimination between each PPA variant and controls, with areas under the curve ranging from 0.87 to 0.97 for sentence comprehension-syntax and from 0.91 to 0.97 for sentence production. However, pairwise comparisons showed no significant differences in discriminative performance among PPA variants after correction for multiple comparisons. Both sentence comprehension-syntax and sentence production showed associations with semantic and repetition measures in addition to motor speech measures. Voxel-based morphometry showed that higher sentence comprehension-syntax scores were associated with greater grey matter volume in left frontotemporal and cingulate regions, whereas higher sentence production scores were additionally associated with greater gray matter volume in frontostriatal structures, including the caudate, putamen, and thalamus. Syntactic processing impairment in Chinese-speaking individuals with PPA extends beyond the nonfluent/agrammatic variant and is associated with distributed frontotemporal and frontostriatal regions, as well as lexical-semantic and auditory verbal short term memory mechanisms. These findings suggest that the cognitive and neural manifestations of syntactic impairment may be shaped by language-specific typological properties, underscoring the need for linguistically informed approaches to the assessment and interpretation of PPA.

title: Clinicopathologic Predictors of PSMA-PET Detection, Recurrence Pattern, and Biochemical Outcome Following Salvage Radiotherapy After Radical Prostatectomy
abstract: Purpose Biochemical recurrence (BCR) after radical prostatectomy (RP) presents heterogeneous recurrence patterns and variable outcomes following salvage radiotherapy (sRT). We evaluated clinicopathologic determinants of PSMA-PET/CT detection, anatomical recurrence distribution, and biochemical disease-free survival (bDFS) following PSMA-PET-guided sRT. Methods This retrospective single-institution study included 140 patients with BCR after RP who underwent 68 Ga-PSMA-PET/CT prior to sRT with or without androgen deprivation therapy. PSMA-PET-positive findings were categorized as prostate bed only (PBO) or pelvic nodal involvement with or without the prostate bed (PLNI). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, logistic regression, and Cox proportional hazards models were employed. Results PSMA-PET detected locoregional recurrence in 77/140 patients (55%). On multivariable analysis, PSA at recurrence (OR=2.07; p=0.003) and age (OR=1.07; p=0.016) were the sole independent predictors of PSMA-PET positivity. ROC analysis yielded AUC=0.74 (optimal threshold of 0.58 ng/mL). Among PSMA-positive patients, PBO was associated with a longer time to BCR (tBCR) (37.5 versus 15 months; p=0.006). Seminal vesicle invasion (SVI) and pT-stage predicted PLNI on univariable analysis. Among 124 of 140 evaluable patients (median follow-up 31 months), estimated bDFS at 24, 36, and 60 months was 89.7%, 80.2%, and 54.1%, respectively. SVI (HR=2.39; p=0.031), EPE (HR=2.82; p=0.012), pT-stage (HR=1.64; p=0.021), and pN-stage (HR=1.83; p=0.045) were associated with increased failure on univariable Cox regression, though none retained independent significance. Conclusion PSA burden and age independently predicted PSMA-PET detection. Recurrence patterns reflected disease behavior, as PBO was associated with longer tBCR. Adverse pathologic features were associated with pelvic nodal disease and reduced biochemical control; none remained independently predictive.

title: Deep Learning-Based Anatomical Level Classification of Craniofacial CT Slices: Comparison of CNN Architectures and Ensemble Methods
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) interpretation requires recognition of the anatomical level of each slice. Classification may facilitate preprocessing and AI-assisted fracture diagnosis. We developed deep learning models to classify craniofacial CT slices into six anatomical categories. A total of 11,769 images were collected from a multicenter database involving 10 Japanese university hospitals and the public Head-Neck-Radiomics-HN1 dataset. Patients were divided into training (70%) and evaluation (30%) sets. Five CNN architectures were trained from scratch, and hard- and soft-voting ensembles were evaluated. Individual-model accuracy ranged from 94.72% to 96.09%; the hard-voting ensemble achieved 96.46% accuracy (Cohens {kappa} = 0.954). Although performance differed among individual models (Cochrans Q = 99.29, p < 0.001), the ensemble did not significantly outperform EfficientNetV2B1 (McNemars p = 0.163). Errors occurred mainly between adjacent anatomical regions. Deep learning can classify craniofacial CT slices accurately and may support automated dataset organization and AI-assisted fracture diagnosis. External validation is needed.

title: Neurochemical fingerprinting of the Alzheimers disease continuum using 7 T short-echo-time brain single voxel 1H-MRS.
abstract: IntroductionThis study aimed to characterize the neurochemical profile of Alzheimers disease (AD) continuum stages using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS) data for brain metabolites and macromolecules. We used Orthogonal Projection to Latent Structures Discriminant Analysis (OPLS-DA) to classify diagnostic groups and assess feature importance. MethodsOur dataset consisted of 7 T short-echo time 1H-MRS spectra of the posterior cingulate cortex/precuneus of individuals diagnosed with AD (n = 27) or Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI, n = 27) and Healthy Controls (HC, n = 31). Classification used 100-round Monte Carlo cross-validation based on metabolite concentrations and macromolecular peak intensities. Variable importance in projection (VIP) was assessed across classification models to identify the most relevant neurochemical features. The resulting metabolite rankings were compared with previous literature to evaluate their biological plausibility. ResultsClassification was strongest for AD versus HC (AUC=0.88) and lower for comparisons involving MCI. Metabolites contributing most strongly to classification included myo-inositol, ascorbate, and choline-containing compounds, consistent with previous studies on AD-related neurochemical alterations. In addition, specific macromolecular components were identified as relevant features, suggesting a potential contribution of MM signals to the characterization of AD-related neurochemistry. DiscussionThese findings support the use of short-echo-time 1H-MRS as a complementary tool for characterizing neurochemical changes in the AD continuum, with potential applications in disease characterization and monitoring, warranting validation in larger cohorts.

title: Preclinical Evaluation of [ 18 F]Itareparib, a brain penetrant PARP1-selective radioligand, in Glioma Rat Model and Nonhuman Primate
abstract: ABSTRACT Rationale Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase-1 (PARP1) is a central mediator of DNA damage response and is upregulated in glioma, supporting it as a molecular imaging biomarker. However, quantitative PET assessment of PARP1 in infiltrative tumors with a preserved blood-brain barrier remains an unmet need. In this study, we evaluated if [ 18 F]Itareparib, a brain-penetrant, non-trapping, PARP1-selective radioligand with reversible kinetics, could improve brain tumor diagnosis and enable target occupancy studies in neurooncology. Methods [ 18 F]Itareparib was synthesized and evaluated in an orthotopic rat model of BT142 IDH1-mutant gliomas. Dynamic PET scans were performed with or without the administration of the PARP1-selective inhibitor AZD9574. Standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs) for tumors were calculated using the contralateral region as reference and compared with distribution volume ratios (DVRs) calculated using kinetic modeling. PARP1-specific binding and tracer stability were assessed using autoradiography, immunofluorescence, biodistribution, and radiometabolite analysis. Brain kinetics of [ 18 F]Itareparib were evaluated in a healthy nonhuman primate (NHP) at baseline and blocking conditions. Results [ 18 F]Itareparib rapidly entered the rat brains and showed 4-fold higher uptake in BT142 tumors than in the contralateral brain. AZD9574 reduced tumor uptake by 77%, supporting the PARP1-specific binding of [ 18 F]Itareparib in the tumors. SUVR (30–60 min) showed the closest agreement with DVR. Autoradiographic tumor-to-reference mean ratio was 7.3, and AZD9574 reduced the tumor-to-reference ratio by 56%. PARP1 immunofluorescence was higher in tumor than the rest of the brain and correlated with autoradiographic results. In rats, the parent fraction of [ 18 F]Itareparib exceeded 99% in brain through 60 min post tracer injection ( p.i. ) and was approximately 88% in plasma at 60 min p.i. In the NHP, [ 18 F]Itareparib showed rapid brain uptake, and V T decreased by 21 ± 6 % after blocking with AZD9574. Conclusion [ 18 F]Itareparib showed brain penetration, high in vivo metabolic stability, reversible binding kinetics, and PARP1-specific tumor uptake. These findings support further development of [ 18 F]Itareparib for the quantitative PET imaging of PARP1 in brain tumors.

ABSTRACT

Rationale

Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase-1 (PARP1) is a central mediator of DNA damage response and is upregulated in glioma, supporting it as a molecular imaging biomarker. However, quantitative PET assessment of PARP1 in infiltrative tumors with a preserved blood-brain barrier remains an unmet need. In this study, we evaluated if [ 18 F]Itareparib, a brain-penetrant, non-trapping, PARP1-selective radioligand with reversible kinetics, could improve brain tumor diagnosis and enable target occupancy studies in neurooncology.

Methods

[ 18 F]Itareparib was synthesized and evaluated in an orthotopic rat model of BT142 IDH1-mutant gliomas. Dynamic PET scans were performed with or without the administration of the PARP1-selective inhibitor AZD9574. Standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs) for tumors were calculated using the contralateral region as reference and compared with distribution volume ratios (DVRs) calculated using kinetic modeling. PARP1-specific binding and tracer stability were assessed using autoradiography, immunofluorescence, biodistribution, and radiometabolite analysis. Brain kinetics of [ 18 F]Itareparib were evaluated in a healthy nonhuman primate (NHP) at baseline and blocking conditions.

Results

[ 18 F]Itareparib rapidly entered the rat brains and showed 4-fold higher uptake in BT142 tumors than in the contralateral brain. AZD9574 reduced tumor uptake by 77%, supporting the PARP1-specific binding of [ 18 F]Itareparib in the tumors. SUVR (30–60 min) showed the closest agreement with DVR. Autoradiographic tumor-to-reference mean ratio was 7.3, and AZD9574 reduced the tumor-to-reference ratio by 56%. PARP1 immunofluorescence was higher in tumor than the rest of the brain and correlated with autoradiographic results. In rats, the parent fraction of [ 18 F]Itareparib exceeded 99% in brain through 60 min post tracer injection ( p.i. ) and was approximately 88% in plasma at 60 min p.i. In the NHP, [ 18 F]Itareparib showed rapid brain uptake, and V T decreased by 21 ± 6 % after blocking with AZD9574.

Conclusion

[ 18 F]Itareparib showed brain penetration, high in vivo metabolic stability, reversible binding kinetics, and PARP1-specific tumor uptake. These findings support further development of [ 18 F]Itareparib for the quantitative PET imaging of PARP1 in brain tumors.

title: TiSAM: fusing spatial and histopathology foundation models for whole-slide image segmentation
abstract: Semantic segmentation of whole-slide images (WSIs) quantifies tissue composition and architecture, but existing models require extensive annotation and lose accuracy as the number of tissue classes increases or on heterogeneous, cross-scanner datasets. Here, we present the Tissue Segment Anything Model (TiSAM), which fuses SAM3 spatial features with UNI2-h pathology features within a multi-scale decoder. Because public benchmarks contain few tissue classes, we release MegaMouse, comprising 36,833 annotations of 52 tissue classes from 12 mouse organs, and an 11-class human pancreas dataset. TiSAM achieved the highest overall performance across four public datasets compared to existing convolutional neural network and vision transformer models, maintained high accuracy on MegaMouse, and maintained high accuracy in the human pancreas dataset when trained on as few as 5 annotated WSIs where previous integrations of SAM with pathology foundation models did not. TiSAM segmentations were also more consistent across eight slide scanners compared to other models. These results establish TiSAM as a general and highly adaptable framework for tissue segmentation, enabling studies containing many tissue classes, limited annotations, or images from multiple scanners.

title: Clinical referral text overrides MRI evidence in multimodal large language models: glioma versus brain abscess
abstract: ObjectivesTo determine how strongly clinical referral text, rather than image content, drives the decisions of multimodal large language models (LLMs) differentiating glioma from brain abscess on MRI. Materials and methodsThis retrospective single-center study included 60 contrast-enhanced T1-weighted brain MRI examinations (30 gliomas, 30 abscesses; reference-standard diagnosis). One axial slice per case was paired with five referral texts (explicitly inflammatory to explicitly tumor-suggestive) under three prompt instructions and submitted 20 times each to GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 5, Gemini 3.5 Flash, and Qwen 3.6 (72,000 answers). The primary outcome was the text-driven span (difference in tumor-call frequency between explicit inflammatory and explicit tumor text). Two blinded radiologists classified the images without text; sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were compared descriptively. ResultsPatients (29 women) had a mean age of 55.8 {+/-} 16.4 years. With neutral text, models answered tumor in 45-67% of queries (specificity, 0.38-0.78), versus 52% and 60% for radiologists (specificity, 0.77 and 0.63). The text-driven span was 0.79-1.00 (p < 0.001 for all models), whereas confirmed gliomas and abscesses differed by only 0.01-0.10 in three models and 0.25 in Gemini 3.5 Flash. Subtle wording produced at least 83% of the span in three models. An instruction to ignore the text reduced the span to 0.48-0.70 in three models and to 0.04 in Gemini 3.5 Flash, partly through reversion to a tumor default. Model accuracy was 0.52-0.73 versus 0.78 and 0.73 for radiologists. ConclusionMultimodal LLMs deferred to referral text over imaging evidence in differentiating glioma from brain abscess, and prompt instructions did not reliably correct this. Key PointsO_ST_ABSQuestionC_ST_ABSMultimodal large language models receive images together with clinical referral text, but how strongly the text rather than the image determines their diagnosis is unknown. FindingsChanging only the referral text largely reversed the glioma-versus-abscess decision for identical MRI images in four models; instructions to ignore the text reduced this inconsistently. Clinical relevanceBefore clinical use, multimodal large language models require model- and task-specific testing of their susceptibility to referral text, because instructing them to prioritize the image is not a dependable safeguard against text-driven misdiagnosis.

title: Beyond Segmentation Accuracy: Evaluating Biological Fidelity in Spatial Pathology
abstract: Multiplex immunofluorescence (MxIF) resolves cellular identity, state, and spatial organization within tumor tissue, enabling higher-order representations of cancer ecosystems including immune infiltration, multicellular neighborhoods, and tissue niches. Yet these analyses depend on a deceptively simple first step: accurately identifying individual cells. Segmentation errors can alter marker quantification, cellular phenotypes, cell–cell relationships, and ultimately the spatial organization inferred from an image. Consequently, improvements in conventional segmentation benchmarks matter biologically only if they propagate to more faithful representations of the tumor microenvironment. We test this relationship directly using an expert-curated benchmark of 31,924 expert-reviewed cells on three slides under a leave-slide-out protocol. We compare a domain-specific self-supervised encoder, adapted to multiplex tissue imaging, with supervised, microscopy-specific, prompted generalist, and general-purpose vision models, and pass every method’s predicted cells through an identical downstream pipeline. We evaluate fidelity across four levels: cell segmentation, phenotype assignment, spatial neighborhood structure, and tissue organization, comprising niches and tumor–immune interactions. The resulting hierarchy reveals that these levels do not improve in lockstep. Cellular phenotype assignment is comparatively robust to segmentation differences, whereas missed cells increasingly disrupt neighborhood structure and tumor–immune interactions. As a stringent spatial-interaction test, tumor–CD8 + contact recovery is poorly predicted by conventional segmentation quality (Panoptic Quality: ρ = 0.18), while errors specifically at tumor–immune interfaces are strongly associated with contact fidelity ( ρ = −0.80). Methods with nearly identical segmentation accuracy can therefore produce substantially different biological representations. These results argue that cell segmentation for spatial pathology should be evaluated not only by boundary and instance accuracy, but also by preservation of the biological relationships that downstream analyses are intended to measure.

title: MoWE: Spatially Adaptive Mixture-of-Wavelet-Experts Pooling for Ultrasound Lesion Segmentation
abstract: We present Mixture-of-Wavelet-Experts (MoWE), a spatially adaptive routing mechanism that replaces max-pooling and strided convolutions in U-Net architectures for ultrasound lesion segmentation. Standard pooling operations suppress high-frequency spatial details, including potential boundary cues in speckled regions. Recent frequency-domain methods preserve some of these details, but a single wavelet family applies the same spectral bias across the image. MoWE instead uses a context-aware router to assign local regions to fixed wavelet families according to local texture and global feature context. The decoder reuses the encoder's spatial routing maps during the inverse transform. Learnable channel-wise gates rescale the high-frequency subbands before reconstruction. We evaluate MoWE with U-Net on four ultrasound lesion benchmarks (BUSI, TN3K, UDIAT, BUS-UCLM) and one cardiac dataset (CAMUS), and with nnU-Net on BUSI. On BUSI, MoWE improves U-Net Dice from 72.59\% to 74.55\% and reduces HD95 from 47.01 to 43.49\,px. With nnU-Net, MoWE improves Dice from 80.18\% to 81.97\% and reduces ASSD from 20.07 to 17.25\,px. On U-Net, MoWE reduces trainable parameters by 6.4\%.

title: CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI
abstract: Pathologic complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy is a key prognostic indicator in aggressive breast cancer, yet existing prediction approaches either rely on pretreatment imaging alone, missing the patient's evolving response, or optimize multi-visit classifiers under direct outcome supervision, coupling representation learning with the clinical endpoint. We formulate longitudinal pCR prediction as a world-modeling problem and propose Conditioned Response-state World Modeling (CoRe-WM), which learns a latent state-transition model that predicts the next imaging state from the observed sequence. The transition function is conditioned on patient clinical profile and assigned therapy through additive shift and feature-wise modulation, enabling patient- and treatment-specific dynamics. A Factorized Response State pathway further decouples treatment-response dynamics from imaging appearance by encoding the structural prior that response manifests primarily in lesion morphology. After pretraining, all parameters are frozen and a linear readout predicts pCR at each clinical decision point. We evaluate CoRe-WM on I-SPY2 under five-fold cross-validation and assess cross-cohort transfer on I-SPY1. CoRe-WM achieves the highest discrimination among all evaluated methods at every prospective decision point, and demonstrates robust cross-cohort transfer. Ablation studies identify patient-profile conditioning and the factorized response pathway as the principal contributors. These results establish world-model-based representation learning as a promising framework for outcome prediction in oncology and beyond.

A Factorized Response State pathway further decouples treatment-response dynamics from imaging appearance by encoding the structural prior that response manifests primarily in lesion morphology. After pretraining, all parameters are frozen and a linear readout predicts pCR at each clinical decision point. We evaluate CoRe-WM on I-SPY2 under five-fold cross-validation and assess cross-cohort transfer on I-SPY1. CoRe-WM achieves the highest discrimination among all evaluated methods at every prospective decision point, and demonstrates robust cross-cohort transfer. Ablation studies identify patient-profile conditioning and the factorized response pathway as the principal contributors. These results establish world-model-based representation learning as a promising framework for outcome prediction in oncology and beyond.

title: Reliability-Preserving Compression for Deployable Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Post-training compression of pretrained medical segmentation models commonly uses quantization, pruning, or distillation to reduce model size and computational cost. Existing medical segmentation quantization studies mainly evaluate Dice, model size, memory, and latency, but this is incomplete for safety-critical use because compressed models should also preserve uncertainty signals that indicate unreliable predictions. We study this problem in compressed MRI/CT segmentation and formalize why Dice can remain stable while uncertainty changes. Motivated by this failure mode, we propose score-guided aggregate-validated mixed precision (SGAV-MP), a post-training compression framework that selects layer precisions under reliability constraints. SGAV-MP ranks quantization actions with a compact benefit-risk score and accepts them only after full-model reliability validation on a calibration set. Across five 2D backbones and three 3D benchmarks, SGAV-MP preserves FP32-level Dice and high uncertainty-map agreement, achieving $3.59\times$--$7.8\times$ compression in 2D and $4.73\times$--$7.82\times$ in 3D. We also report backend-supported TensorRT deployment measurements separately to distinguish runtime execution from reliability-preserving storage compression.

title: Multimodal-Conditioned Latent Diffusion Models for Spatiotemporal Brain MRI Forecasting
abstract: Spatiotemporal forecasting of 3D anatomical changes is a critical generative vision challenge for modeling Alzheimer's Disease (AD) progression. While brain MRI forecasting from single-modality data has advanced, other key complementary multimodal biomarkers remain underutilized. In this work, we propose the Multimodal-Conditioned Latent Diffusion Model (MC-LDM), a novel framework for patient-specific brain MRI synthesis. MC-LDM leverages multimodal biomarkers---MRI, tau-PET, Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR), and APOE4---during training, but relies only on baseline MRI, APOE4, and patient metadata at inference, reflecting realistic clinical availability. Our contributions are threefold: (1) a Latent Diffusion Model (LDM) fine-tuned via Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for data-efficient learning; (2) a multimodal conditioning that integrates molecular and clinical signals to model heterogeneous disease trajectories; and (3) auxiliary predictors estimating unobserved multimodal biomarkers from MRI features and patient covariates to condition the diffusion model, removing the need for these assessments at inference. Trained on 1,355 visits from 852 subjects in the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), MC-LDM reduces average regional volumetric MAE by 18% over the second-best baseline on an independent test set of 664 visits. To our knowledge, MC-LDM represents the first diffusion-based framework to leverage multimodal priors for MRI forecasting. This conceptual advancement enables patient-specific trajectory generation that captures aspects of AD heterogeneity not observable from structural anatomy alone, bridging the gap between rich multimodal supervision and the strict constraints of routine clinical deployment. Code is available at: https://github.com/antonioscardace/MC-LDM.

title: PCXR-Copilot: Device-aware pediatric chest radiographic analysis with segmentation, suppression, and edema-related cues
abstract: Patients admitted to pediatric ICU and cardiac ICU often require intensive perioperative support and frequent chest radiography to monitor support devices, extravascular lung water, and body-wall edema. Radiographic interpretation and analysis is often difficult due to superimposed anatomic and iatrogenic structures that obscure clinically relevant signals. While deep learning can provide decision support, translation to pediatric radiographs is still limited by high device burden and scarcity of pediatric datasets with clinically grounded device annotations. To address this gap, we first introduce PediaDeviceSeg-1K, a curated dataset of 1,000 anterior-posterior radiographs of pediatric CICU patients with clinically grounded, fine-grained annotations of common ICU devices. To our best knowledge, this is the first publicly available pediatric CICU CXR resource with clinically grounded device annotations for device-focused benchmarking. Building on PediaDeviceSeg-1K, we further present PCXR-Copilot, a device-aware pipeline that outputs lung and device masks, optional device-suppressed views, and edema-related visualization maps and scalar indices. The full pipeline has been integrated and runs in real time within the TWIST platform at Boston Children's Hospital, demonstrating feasibility for real-world clinical deployment.

title: SlimFormer++: Token Mixing Where It Matters for Efficient 3D Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: To determine where computation is needed in volumetric segmentation networks, we analyze block-level redundancy and stage-wise token-mixer contribution. Centered Kernel Alignment reveals high input-output representational similarity within blocks of representative convolutional, hybrid, and Transformer-style segmentation networks. Similarity-guided pruning reduces their parameter counts by 39-75% while decreasing mean Dice by less than 0.4 percentage points. To examine token mixers within blocks, we introduce Anatomical Relation Distortion, which quantifies how bypassing a mixer distorts feature relations between labeled anatomical positions. Applied to an unpruned candidate architecture, Centered Kernel Alignment indicates high representational redundancy in intermediate encoder mixers, whereas Anatomical Relation Distortion shows that they contribute little and the bottleneck mixer most. These findings motivate SlimFormer++, which uses Selective Mixing blocks with windowed Mamba mixing in the first encoder stage and only residual channel MLPs in deeper stages. At the bottleneck, Augmented Mixing injects similarity-weighted sparse long-range context into the axial taps of a depthwise convolution at cost linear in voxel count. Evaluated against 12 baselines across eight public CT, MRI, and ultrasound datasets (1,809 cases), SlimFormer++ achieves the highest mean Dice (87.84%) and lowest mean HD95 (6.50 mm) with the fewest parameters (5.98 million). These results support stage-aware token mixing as a design strategy for improving the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in volumetric segmentation. The source code is available at https://github.com/WHHHHHY822/SlimFormerPlusPlus

title: Deep Auxiliary Learning via Bilevel Feature Optimization for Label-Efficient Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Auxiliary learning (AL), which can improve the performance of a primary task by leveraging related auxiliary tasks, is commonly regarded as a special case of multi-task learning. Existing AL approaches typically require manually annotated auxiliary labels, increasing annotation costs, particularly in medical imaging where expert labeling is expensive. In this work, we investigate whether segmentation performance can be improved using auxiliary tasks whose labels are automatically derived from existing segmentation annotations, requiring no additional manual labeling. To address this, we propose a novel auxiliary learning framework, formulated as a bilevel optimization problem. Our method enables effective knowledge transfer between tasks via a feature communication module, enhancing the primary segmentation task. We evaluate the method on three medical image segmentation benchmarks under limited-label settings. The results demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior label efficiency. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/FupingWu90/ALBO.

title: Foundation Model-Enabled Pathology-Informed MRI Model for Preoperative Prediction of Vessels Encapsulating Tumor Clusters in Resectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
abstract: Vessels encapsulating tumor clusters (VETC) are an aggressive vascular phenotype of hepatocellular carcinoma that is usually determined after surgery. A foundation model-enabled framework for pathology-informed VETC prediction on pretreatment magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), termed PIVOT, uses paired preoperative multiparametric MRI, postoperative hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images, and CD34 immunohistochemistry during model development, while inference requires only preoperative MRI. PIVOT-MRI uses morphologic and vascular embedding alignment, and PIVOT-Clinical combines the PIVOT-MRI score with tumor size and alpha-fetoprotein. The multicenter retrospective study includes 2052 patients in a training cohort, an internal test cohort, and four external validation cohorts. PIVOT-MRI achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.887 in the internal test cohort and 0.839-0.861 across external cohorts. PIVOT-Clinical increases the internal-test area under the curve to 0.904 and PIVOT-Clinical-defined groups are associated with different two-year recurrence risks. Removing both histopathologic alignment branches results in the largest ablation-related performance decrease. Exploratory radiotranscriptomic analyses showed that higher PIVOT-MRI scores were associated with angiogenesis-related, endothelial, and proliferative transcriptional programs. PIVOT enables noninvasive preoperative assessment of pathology-defined vascular aggressiveness in resectable hepatocellular carcinoma while preserving an MRI-only clinical inference pathway.

title: Trans-Patch Retrograde Re-Entry During Hybrid Revascularization of an External Iliac Artery Chronic Total Occlusion: A Technical Note and Review of Re-Entry Strategies.
abstract: Failure of true-lumen re-entry after subintimal wire passage is a well-recognized limitation of endovascular treatment for external iliac artery (EIA) chronic total occlusions (CTO). We report a 73-year-old woman with severe limb ischemia and a prior failed endovascular attempt who underwent hybrid left common femoral artery (CFA) endarterectomy with patch angioplasty, followed by trans-patch retrograde access and dedicated device-assisted re-entry (Outback Elite) after antegrade and retrograde wires repeatedly tracked subintimally without reaching the true lumen. Controlled re-entry preserved hypogastric artery flow and allowed drug-eluting stent reconstruction of the EIA. At 12-month follow-up, ABI improved from 0.36 to 0.50, and TBI improved to 0.37. Duplex ultrasound at 6-month follow-up confirmed patency of the reconstructed segment without evidence of hemodynamically significant restenosis. This technical report illustrates the use of an endarterectomized CFA as a retrograde re-entry platform and reviews contemporary strategies for managing subintimal crossing failure in iliac CTOs.

title: Advancing Early Breast Cancer Diagnosis and Ki-67 Expression Prediction With Ultrasound Viscoelastography: Based on Peritumoral Assessment.
abstract: Background Breast cancer is the most common invasive malignancy in women. Ultrasound viscoelastography may improve non-invasive diagnosis, but the clinical relevance of peritumoral viscoelastic parameters (VPs) and their correlation with Ki-67 remain unclear. This study explores these associations. Methods A prospective study enrolled 256 breast masses (156 malignant, 100 benign). Patients underwent conventional ultrasound and viscoelastography. VPs were acquired within masses (A), peritumoral shells (Shell1: 1 mm, Shell2: 2 mm, Shell3: 3 mm), and combined regions (A' = A + Shell). Quantitative metrics included elasticity (V/1 E, V/0 E), dispersion coefficient (V/1 D), viscosity coefficient (V/0 V), and their maximum (Max), minimum (Min), mean(Mean), and standard deviation (SD) values. Diagnostic performance was evaluated by analyzing the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and calculating the area under the curve (AUC), followed by logistic regression. VPs were compared between high/low Ki-67 groups. Results The AUCs of peritumoral VPs exceeded those from masses. V/1 D showed higher AUC than V/0 V and elasticity values, with Shell3 V/1 D SD having the highest AUC (0.840). The diagnostic efficacy of the peritumoral viscoelastic model surpassed that of the single elasticity parameter model, with 89.1% sensitivity, 73% specificity, 82.8% accuracy. Key variables included Shell3 V/1 D and Shell3 V/0 E. Shell1 V/0 V Max was significantly higher in high versus low Ki-67 expression groups ( p < 0.05). Conclusion The viscoelastic model improves diagnostic accuracy by quantifying peritumoral biomechanics, and certain VPs may predict Ki-67 expression. Peritumoral VPs show potential as novel non-invasive imaging biomarkers for early breast cancer evaluation.

title: Histopathological Spectrum in FIT-Positive Patients With Abnormal Colonoscopy Findings at a Tertiary Medical Center in Lebanon: A Retrospective Observational Study.
abstract: Background and aims Colorectal cancer is a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality, and the prognosis significantly depends on the diagnostic stage. Various screening initiatives have been established, among which the fecal immunochemical test (FIT) (FITFIT) which is prominent for its affordability, non-invasive approach, and wide acceptance. This study aimed to describe the spectrum of histopathological findings among patients with positive fecal occult blood test and abnormal colonoscopy findings, and to identify associated risk factors. Methods This retrospective observational study included 172 adults with documented positive FIT and abnormal colonoscopy findings at Makassed General Hospital from January 2024 to December 2025. Statistical analysis was conducted using SPSS version 25, and associations were assessed using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, with significance defined as p < 0.05. Results A total of 172 patients were included, with a mean age of 63.88 ± 11.79 years, and 55.2% were female. The most frequently recorded indications for colonoscopy were anemia (39%) and screening (37.2%). Polyps were the most common colonoscopy finding. Histopathological examination demonstrated that neoplastic polyps represented the predominant diagnosis (65.1%), followed by non-neoplastic lesions (24.4%) and malignancy (10.5%). Patients aged 45 years and older demonstrated a higher prevalence of polyps on colonoscopy; however, the difference did not reach statistical significance. No significant association was observed between gender and colonoscopy or histopathological findings. Abdominal pain and diarrhea were both significantly associated with non-neoplastic histopathological lesions. Conclusion Among patients with positive FIT and abnormal colonoscopy findings, neoplastic polyps rather than malignancy represented the predominant histopathological findings, supporting the clinical utility of FIT in detecting clinically important colorectal lesions at earlier stages. In addition, variability in the histopathology depending on the clinical presentation may contribute to clinical assessment and risk stratification. Larger prospective studies are needed to determine predictors of advanced colorectal histopathology.

title: Defining the Clinical Indication for Real-Time Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Ultrasound in Breast Lesions with Low Suspicion of Malignancy.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate whether real-time artificial intelligence (AI) breast ultrasound (US) can identify a subgroup of breast imaging reporting and data system (BI-RADS) category 4A lesions without suspicious mammographic (MMG) findings in whom unnecessary biopsy may be safely avoided. Methods This retrospective analysis of single-center biopsy registry included 641 consecutive US BI-RADS 4A lesions that underwent vacuum-assisted breast biopsy. Before conducting biopsy, the lesions were reassessed using a real-time AI US system (CadAI-B®), and MMG findings were classified as suspicious or non-suspicious based on formal reports. Seven prespecified biopsy-decision strategies were evaluated, including 3 AI-only strategies, 3 mammography-gated AI strategies, and the current standard strategy of biopsy all BI-RADS 4A lesions. The primary outcomes were biopsy reduction rate, missed cancers, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and accuracy, with final pathology as the reference standard. Results Among 641 cases of US BI-RADS 4A lesions, 26 cases of malignancies (4.1%) were identified, including 14 cases of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), 11 cases of invasive ductal carcinomas, and 1 case of apocrine carcinoma. AI reassigned 289 cases of lesions (45.1%) to BI-RADS categories 1-3. AI-only biopsy-deferral strategies missed 30.8% and 38.5% of malignancies when biopsy was deferred for AI BI-RADS ≤2 and ≤3 lesions, respectively, with DCIS accounting for most missed cancers. In contrast, among lesions without suspicious MMG findings, no malignancies were observed in AI BI-RADS 1-3 lesions. The sequential strategy of deferring biopsy only for lesions with AI BI-RADS ≤3 and non-suspicious MMG findings reduced biopsies by 43.5% (279/641) while maintaining 100.0% sensitivity (95% CI, 87.1-100.0%) and increasing specificity to 45.4% (95% CI, 41.4-49.4%). Conclusion Real-time AI breast US alone could not safely support biopsy deferral in US BI-RADS 4A lesions. However, after suspicious MMG findings had been excluded, AI identified a low-risk subgroup in whom unnecessary biopsy could be substantially reduced without compromising cancer detection. These findings suggest that the clinical utility of real-time AI breast US lies in patients without suspicious MMG findings. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

title: Asymptomatic Portomesenteric Venous Thrombosis After Colorectal Cancer Surgery: Incidence, Natural History, and Implications for Management.
abstract: Background Portomesenteric venous thrombosis (PMVT) after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery is most often reported in symptomatic patients, leaving its frequency and natural history across the asymptomatic spectrum poorly defined. When encountered incidentally, it frequently prompts anticoagulation, hypercoagulability evaluation, or delays in oncologic treatment, despite limited evidence that intervention alters its course. Using a cohort with routine postoperative imaging, we characterized the incidence, anatomic distribution, risk factors, and clinical course of asymptomatic PMVT. Methods We retrospectively studied 799 consecutive patients who underwent CRC surgery between April 2019 and June 2025. All patients underwent standardized abdominal computed tomography (CT) on postoperative day (POD) 6 as part of our institutional clinical pathway for immediate postoperative follow-up. PMVT was defined radiologically, and thrombus location was classified as peripheral intrahepatic branches or main portal/superior mesenteric vein. Management followed a risk-stratified pathway of therapeutic anticoagulation or active surveillance, with radiologic resolution assessed on follow-up CT. Given the limited number of events, multivariable analysis was considered exploratory. Results Asymptomatic PMVT was identified in 33 patients (4.1%), none symptomatic at detection. Thrombi were predominantly confined to the distal intrahepatic branches. In exploratory multivariable analysis, age ≤ 60 years (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.19-5.03, p = 0.015) and POD 5 WBC > 10 × 10 9 /L (OR 2.39, 95% CI 1.16-4.93, p = 0.018) were independently associated with PMVT. Twenty-one patients received anticoagulation and 12 were managed with surveillance alone. Complete radiologic resolution occurred in all 33 patients within one year, including every patient managed without anticoagulation. Furthermore, there were no cases of thrombus extension, portal hypertension, or bowel ischemia. Conclusion When postoperative imaging is routinely performed, asymptomatic PMVT after CRC surgery is detected in approximately 4% of patients. It is typically confined to peripheral intrahepatic branches, and follows a uniformly benign self-limiting course, even in patients managed without anticoagulation. These findings argue against reflexive anticoagulation and extensive workup for short-segment, non-occlusive PMVT confined to peripheral intrahepatic branches, and support an individualized, predominantly conservative approach. We do not advocate routine postoperative CT; rather, surgeons who encounter incidental PMVT can be reassured regarding its favorable prognosis.

title: Awareness, need and utilization of breast cancer risk management resources in women with hereditary cancer susceptibility.
abstract: Background Germline genetic testing is increasing. While testing barriers are well characterized, less is known about post-testing needs and utilization of screening and prevention resources by women with pathogenic variants (PVs) in breast cancer susceptibility genes. Methods A 38-question online survey was developed by Facing Our Risk of Cancer Empowered (FORCE), a patient advocacy group, and administered electronically to subscribers from February-May 2024. Study eligibility criteria included female sex and a germline PV conferring elevated lifetime risk of breast cancer (ATM, BARD1, BRCA1, BRCA2, CDH1, CHEK2, PALB2, PTEN, RAD51C, RAD51D, STK11, or TP53). Results Of 1,025 respondents who initiated the survey, 937 were women. Most were non-Hispanic White (91.7%) and from the United States (81.6%). The most common PVs were BRCA2 (31.4%), BRCA1 (25.5%) and CHEK2 (9.2%). The most frequently used resources were education and information services about medical options (39.3%) and peer support (28.1%). Few respondents used financial navigation (4.0%) or financial support (5.3%), but up to 45% reported needing these services. Among breast screening users (53.8% used mammogram, 42.2% magnetic resonance imaging, 19.4% ultrasound), 37.8% found it hard to prepare emotionally for results and 14% found it hard to pay for screening. One-third (37.1%) of respondents found deciding whether to have risk-reducing mastectomy hard; two-thirds (64.0%) found physical recovery hard, more than half (60.2%) found emotional recovery hard, and one-quarter (24.7%) found paying for risk-reducing mastectomy hard. Conclusion In this contemporary sample of women at elevated risk of breast cancer, more than one-third had unmet financial needs and up to two-thirds had difficulty with screening or risk-reducing surgery. Closing these gaps will be essential to improve outcomes for women with hereditary breast cancer.

title: Morphometric analysis and three-dimensional reconstruction of sphenoid sinus: Associations of linear dimensions and volume with pneumatization patterns and neurovascular relationships.
abstract: Background The sphenoid sinus (SS) shows morphological variability relevant to endoscopic endonasal skull-base access. This study examined associations of SS volume and linear dimensions with pneumatization patterns, extensions, and neurovascular anatomy. Methods This retrospective study included 253 adult sinus computed tomography (CT) examinations. Μaximum anteroposterior (AP max), laterolateral (LL max), and craniocaudal (CC max) dimensions were measured, and SS volume was calculated by semi-automated three-dimensional contouring with manual refinement. Pneumatization patterns and relationships with the internal carotid artery (ICA), optic nerve (ON), and Vidian nerve (VN) were examined using exploratory univariable logistic regression, supplemented by separate age- and sex-adjusted models for neurovascular outcomes. Results Mean SS volume was 11.12 ± 4.50 cm³. Males had greater volume (p = 0.001) and AP max (p = 0.013) than females. Volume correlated strongly with LL max (r = 0.791) and AP max (r = 0.705) (both p < 0.001). Each 1-mm increase in AP max was associated with posterior extension (OR = 1.57, 95% CI 1.40-1.76) and ICA (OR = 1.22), ON (OR = 1.13), and VN (OR = 1.24) protrusion and/or dehiscence. Each 1-mm increase in LL max was associated with lateral extension (OR = 1.39, 95% CI 1.28-1.52) and VN protrusion and/or dehiscence (OR = 1.24, 95% CI 1.18-1.31) (p < 0.001). Greater SS volume was associated with protrusion and/or dehiscence of all three structures, and remained associated with these neurovascular outcomes after adjustment for age and sex. Conclusions SS volume and linear dimensions provide complementary quantitative information on the magnitude and direction of pneumatization. AP max and LL max were associated with specific extension patterns and with neurovascular protrusion and/or dehiscence.

title: Clinical phenotype and bone microarchitecture of cutaneous-skeletal hypophosphatemia syndrome: experience from a single center in China.
abstract: Context Cutaneous-skeletal hypophosphatemia syndrome (CSHS) is a rare mosaic RASopathy characterized by epidermal or melanocytic nevi, skeletal dysplasia, and fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23)-mediated hypophosphatemic rickets. However, its bone microarchitectural features remain underdefined. Objectives The study aimed to characterize the clinical, genetic, and skeletal microarchitectural features of CSHS. Methods We summarized clinical findings of 6 CSHS patients with genetically confirmed somatic RAS mutations. Skeletal involvement was assessed by whole-body bone scintigraphy. High-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography parameters at the distal radius and tibia were compared with age- and sex-matched XLH controls (1:3). Literature review of 24 genetically confirmed CSHS patients was performed to assess genotype-phenotype correlation. Results All patients were confirmed to carry somatic HRAS or NRAS mutation in affected skin. Hypophosphatemia, elevated alkaline phosphatase and elevated FGF23 were found in all patients. Genotype-phenotype correlation analysis did not identify any significant biochemical or systemic burden differences across 3 genotypes. Compared with XLH controls, CSHS patients exhibited significantly reduced total and trabecular volumetric BMD (vBMD), with relatively preserved cortical vBMD. Bone cross-sectional geometry was less expanded than in XLH at the tibia. In addition, thinner trabeculae with greater separation were found at the radius, and the distal tibia showed thinner cortices and decreased cortical porosity. Estimated bone stiffness and failure load were significantly lower at both the radius and tibia. Conclusions CSHS is associated with pronounced trabecular vBMD impairment and reduced bone strength compared with XLH controls. These findings are consistent with a combined contribution of intrinsic skeletal dysplasia and chronic hypophosphatemia on bone, although further studies are needed to elucidate these mechanisms.

title: Preliminary study on early microvascular ingrowth into distracted callus during distraction osteogenesis-A non-invasive approach to explore the early growth patterns and possible mechanism of distraction osteogenesis in vivo.
abstract: Background Distraction osteogenesis (DO) is critical for repairing large segmental bone defects. Early callus vascularization is essential for bone regeneration; however, real-time microcirculatory assessment remains lacking. This study aimed to elucidate spatiotemporal microvascular network construction in distracted callus using super-resolution contrast-enhanced ultrasound (SR CEUS) and high-frame-rate contrast-enhanced ultrasound (HiFR CEUS) in a sheep tibial DO model. Methods Six sheep underwent tibial DO. On day 7 of distraction, B-mode ultrasound, "Firefly" imaging, SR CEUS, and HiFR CEUS were performed. Quantitative parameters including vessel density (VD), perfusion index (PI), mean intensity, and peak intensity (PKI) were compared among three regions: central high-perfusion area (CHPA), annular low-perfusion area (ALPA), and peripheral high-perfusion area (PHPA). Results B-mode ultrasound revealed outward bulging of distracted callus. "Firefly" imaging detected microcalcifications. SR CEUS showed PHPA (67.58% of cross-sectional area) received centripetal blood flow from periosteum and surrounding soft tissues; CHPA (10.39%) received centrifugal flow from the medullary cavity; ALPA (22.03%), located between them, exhibited significantly lower mean intensity than CHPA/PHPA and significantly lower VD and PI than PHPA (P < 0.05). HiFR CEUS showed perfusion appeared first in CHPA, then PHPA, and lastly ALPA. Conclusion SR and HiFR CEUS enable non-invasive, dynamic visualization and quantification of microvascular growth in distracted callus, revealing a "target ring sign", "bidirectional fusion" perfusion pattern, and "central-first, peripheral-second" perfusion sequence. ALPA was identified as a hypovascular zone potentially associated with delayed mineralization or cyst formation. This system provides a novel imaging framework for early assessment of callus viability, prediction of osteogenic risk, and guidance of individualized distraction strategies.

Background

Distraction osteogenesis (DO) is critical for repairing large segmental bone defects. Early callus vascularization is essential for bone regeneration; however, real-time microcirculatory assessment remains lacking. This study aimed to elucidate spatiotemporal microvascular network construction in distracted callus using super-resolution contrast-enhanced ultrasound (SR CEUS) and high-frame-rate contrast-enhanced ultrasound (HiFR CEUS) in a sheep tibial DO model.

Methods

Six sheep underwent tibial DO. On day 7 of distraction, B-mode ultrasound, "Firefly" imaging, SR CEUS, and HiFR CEUS were performed. Quantitative parameters including vessel density (VD), perfusion index (PI), mean intensity, and peak intensity (PKI) were compared among three regions: central high-perfusion area (CHPA), annular low-perfusion area (ALPA), and peripheral high-perfusion area (PHPA).

Results

B-mode ultrasound revealed outward bulging of distracted callus. "Firefly" imaging detected microcalcifications. SR CEUS showed PHPA (67.58% of cross-sectional area) received centripetal blood flow from periosteum and surrounding soft tissues; CHPA (10.39%) received centrifugal flow from the medullary cavity; ALPA (22.03%), located between them, exhibited significantly lower mean intensity than CHPA/PHPA and significantly lower VD and PI than PHPA (P < 0.05). HiFR CEUS showed perfusion appeared first in CHPA, then PHPA, and lastly ALPA.

Conclusion

SR and HiFR CEUS enable non-invasive, dynamic visualization and quantification of microvascular growth in distracted callus, revealing a "target ring sign", "bidirectional fusion" perfusion pattern, and "central-first, peripheral-second" perfusion sequence. ALPA was identified as a hypovascular zone potentially associated with delayed mineralization or cyst formation. This system provides a novel imaging framework for early assessment of callus viability, prediction of osteogenic risk, and guidance of individualized distraction strategies.

title: Multi-center study of CMR versus cardiac catheterization with endomyocardial biopsy for pediatric transplant surveillance: study protocol.
abstract: Notwithstanding advances in post-transplant care, acute allograft rejection (AR) remains the leading cause of mortality in pediatric heart transplant recipients (PHTX). Endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) continues to be the standard of care for AR detection, despite being invasive, costly, and associated with patient discomfort and potential complications. Non-invasive alternatives, including cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) with T1 and T2 parametric mapping and blood biomarkers (BB) such as cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and microRNA (miRNA), have shown promise in the adult transplant population, but their validation in the pediatric transplant population is lacking. The "Predictive Modeling of Acute Rejection in Pediatric Heart Transplant Recipients" (PEACE) study is a prospective, multicenter trial aiming to assess the diagnostic accuracy of CMR and BB in comparison to EMB. The goal of this manuscript is to describe the purpose and experimental protocol of the PEACE study. The PEACE study's overarching hypothesis is that CMR and BB can consistently and accurately detect myocardial abnormalities, potentially guiding the need for EMB. Secondary objectives include cost-analyses of CMR and BB, as well as a biomarker performance evaluation in biopsy-negative, but symptomatic and suspected AR cases. PEACE will enroll PHTX ages 6-25 years, across approximately 20 U.S. pediatric hospitals. All subjects will undergo EMB for surveillance or suspected AR as standard of care. As part of the research protocol, subjects will undergo blood collection for BB prior to the EMB and CMR within 5 days of EMB. Central core labs will conduct blinded analysis for imaging, pathology, and biomarkers to ensure consistent data interpretation. PEACE represents a critical step in reducing reliance on invasive biopsies in the clinical care of PHTX. By validating non-invasive tools in a large, diverse population, the PEACE study could transform AR detection, resulting in improvement of the patient experience and outcomes in this vulnerable population. (Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07770659, Non-invasive Prediction of EArly Cardiac rEjection (PEACE)).

title: Adaptive local region super-resolution for high-field MRI: A diffusion-based approach with structural and frequency-domain constraints.
abstract: High-field MRI offers superior SNR but is constrained by the trade-off between spatial resolution and acquisition time. Existing global deep learning super-resolution (SR) methods often incur computational overhead by ignoring regional image content. This motivates an adaptive local SR strategy to optimize efficiency and detail preservation. To address this, we developed a local SR method that adaptively allocates computational resources to information-rich regions. The proposed framework regularized an entropy-based local region processing strategy with a diffusion model fortified by frequency-domain and structural constraints. We retrospectively evaluated our method on two diverse datasets: a proprietary 7.0 T dental MRI dataset (25 T2-weighted DESS sequences from 10 beagle dogs) and a public 5.0 T brain MRI dataset (Diff5T, 50 diffusion-weighted sequences). Image quality was quantified using PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and FID. On the 7.0 T dental test dataset (2 subjects), our method achieved a PSNR of 27.31 [26.83, 27.79] dB and the lowest LPIPS of 0.19 [0.18, 0.20]. On the 5.0 T brain test dataset (10 subjects), the method achieved a PSNR of 27.15 ± 0.10 dB, an LPIPS of 0.14 ± 0.00 and an FID of 54.01, with lower perceptual metrics than the evaluated baselines. Ablation studies indicated that the proposed frequency-domain and structural constraints reduced LPIPS and FID, with trade-offs in PSNR and SSIM. In conclusion, the evaluated framework showed improvements in perceptual metrics by integrating targeted local processing with frequency-domain and structural regularization, accompanied by a trade-off in pixel-wise fidelity metrics, supporting the technical feasibility of addressing the resolution-time trade-off in high-field MRI. Future work will focus on expanding the dataset and evaluating the framework in human dental cohorts to address anatomical differences between the current canine model and human dental anatomy.

title: CAG repeat length shapes bidirectional functional connectome alterations in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3: a multimodal MRI study.
abstract: The ATXN3 gene is the primary driver of brain damage in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3). We aimed to elucidate the patterns of connectome alterations shaped by cytosine-adenine-guanine (CAG) repeat length in SCA3. Eighty-nine genetically confirmed patients with SCA3 and 89 age-, sex-, education-matched healthy controls underwent multimodal MRI and comprehensive clinical assessments. Connectome-based predictive modeling (CPM) was used to identify functional connectivity patterns associated with CAG repeat length. Structural brain damage was assessed using voxel-based morphometry. Mediation analysis was performed to examine the role of structural impairment in connectivity changes. CPM identified a positive and a negative network, whose connectivity strength increased or decreased with CAG repeat length. The positive network (r = 0.397, P < 0.001) was mainly localized within the cerebello-motor circuit and was positively associated with ataxia severity and functional disability. The negative network (r = 0.243, P = 0.022) was distributed across large-scale networks, with selective vulnerability of interhemispheric connectivity, and was associated with motor dysfunction. Besides the canonical motor pathways, limbic-related connectivity was related to motor impairment. Structural analyses revealed widespread gray matter atrophy centered on the cerebellum. Cerebellar atrophy statistically mediated the association between CAG repeat length and connectivity decreases. CAG repeat length is associated with a bidirectional connectopathy in SCA3. Cerebellar atrophy may mediate the connectivity decreases. Future longitudinal studies are required to examine the underlying causal pathway.

title: The PENIMA project: artificial intelligence decision-support tool for penile lesions - protocol paper and invitation to participate.
abstract: Objectives To present and describe the design, data collection framework, and interim cohort characteristics of the PENIMA project, a multicentre initiative establishing a clinically annotated penile lesion image repository to support future artificial intelligence (AI)-driven decision-support development - and to encourage urology and dermatology colleagues working with penile lesions to participate in the project. Patients and methods Prospective participant inclusion commenced in March 2023 across Scandinavian urological and dermatological departments. Patients with penile anatomy undergoing clinically indicated genital examination are invited to participate and provide oral and written consent as defined by local authority regulations. Clinical photographs and structured metadata are collected. Lesion classification is based on a specialist evaluation, clinical follow-up and histopathology when available. Images are pseudonymised and annotated using a secure, containerised Computer Vision Annotation Tool (CVAT) environment. Supervised machine-learning model development using convolutional neural networks is planned with patient-level dataset partitioning and evaluation using standard diagnostic performance metrics. The study was approved by relevant local authorities, and the approval number is 1-10-72-150-22. Results As of February 2026, 1125 participants and approximately 7000 images have been included. In all, 40% represented normal anatomical variants. Among lesional cases, 33% are clinically assessed as benign, 13% premalignant, and 8% malignant; 22% of all cases have histopathological verification. Concordance between clinical suspicion and histopathology is highest for penile carcinoma (84.6%, 95% confidence interval 75.0-91.0%). Conclusion The PENIMA project includes a multicentre, clinically grounded image repository reflecting real-world penile lesion presentations. The feasible and successful infrastructure provides a foundation for future development and validation of image-based clinical decision-support tools.

title: Segment-based comparison of multiparametric MRI, Gallium-68-PSMA-PET/CT and combined imaging with histopathology in prostate cancer.
abstract: Objectives To compare the segment-based diagnostic performance of multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI), Gallium-68-prostate-specific membrane antigen-positron emission tomography/computed tomography ( 68 Ga-PSMA-PET/CT), for detecting histopathologically confirmed prostate cancer (PCa). Patients and methods This analysis included 97 men from the prospective, interventional, phase II DEPROMP (DEtection rate of clinically significant PROstate cancer by mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT fusion biopsy) trial who underwent radical prostatectomy with whole-mount histopathological evaluation. All participants received mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT prior to biopsy. The mpMRI was interpreted according to Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) version(v)2.1, and PSMA-PET/CT according to Prostate Cancer Molecular Imaging Standardised Evaluation (PROMISE) molecular imaging Tumour-Node-Metastasis (miTNM) criteria. The prostate was divided into 36 anatomical segments based on the PI-RADS v2.1 sector map. Each segment was correlated with histopathological findings from prostatectomy specimens. For each imaging modality, detection rates, sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were calculated at the segment level. Results A total of 3492 prostate segments were analysed. Detection rates were 74.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 72.6-75.5) for mpMRI, 72.2% (95% CI 70.6-73.6) for PSMA-PET/CT, and 79.1% (95% CI 77.7-80.4) for the combined use of mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT. Sensitivity and specificity were 13.4% and 97.3% for mpMRI, 18.5% and 92.7% for PSMA-PET/CT, and 25.8% and 90.5% for combined mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT, respectively. Threshold-based receiver operating characteristic analyses yielded an AUC of 0.62 (95% CI 0.54-0.69) for PI-RADS, 0.68 (95% CI 0.63-0.74) for maximum standardised uptake value, and 0.69 (95% CI 0.65-0.74) for molecular imaging PSMA. Conclusion At the segment level, mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT showed comparable diagnostic accuracy with high specificity but limited sensitivity. Their combination improved sensitivity and overall detection performance, underscoring the complementary value of structural and molecular imaging for lesion localisation and precision management in PCa.

title: Transient apnoea for motion control during flexible ureteroscopic lithotripsy: a randomised trial.
abstract: Objectives To determine whether transient apnoea (TA) during flexible ureteroscopic laser lithotripsy improves active lithotripsy efficiency compared with regular mechanical ventilation (RMV) and small tidal-volume ventilation (STVV). Patients and methods In this single-centre, three-arm randomised trial, 150 adults with a single computed tomography (CT)-confirmed renal, ureteropelvic, or proximal ureteric stone measuring 10-<20 mm were assigned one-to-one-to-one to RMV, STVV, or TA. TA followed 5-min 100% oxygen pre-oxygenation, with 9-min maximum and pre-specified stopping criteria under continuous anaesthetic monitoring. The primary endpoint was active lithotripsy efficiency, defined as CT-estimated stone volume divided by elapsed active lithotripsy time. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle. Results The mean (standard deviation) active lithotripsy efficiency was 27.8 (8.9), 26.6 (8.0), and 34.3 (10.0) mm 3 /min with RMV, STVV, and TA, respectively (P < 0.001). TA increased adjusted efficiency by 5.9 mm 3 /min vs RMV (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.2-9.6 mm 3 /min) and 6.8 mm 3 /min vs STVV (95% CI 3.3-10.2 mm 3 /min). The median active lithotripsy time was 27.5, 26.5, and 22.0 min (P = 0.001); total operative time was 50.0, 50.0, and 43.0 min (P = 0.002); and surgeon-rated targeting stability scores were 7.0, 7.0, and 9.0 (P < 0.001), respectively. Postoperative Day 1/1-month stone-free rates were 88%/92%, 80%/96%, and 88%/90%, respectively, with no significant between-group differences. The median (interquartile range) achieved apnoea duration was 5.0 (4.5-6.8) min; 46/50 resumed ventilation before the 9-min maximum, most commonly for heart-rate decline/bradycardia (n = 27) or blood-pressure decline/hypotension (n = 20). No patient had a peripheral oxygen saturation <90% or a Clavien-Dindo Grade ≥III complication; transient hypercapnia and respiratory acidosis improved after ventilation resumed. Conclusion Transient apnoea improved lithotripsy efficiency and shortened operative time compared with RMV and STVV, with higher surgeon-rated targeting stability. The benefit was primarily intraoperative, without evidence of greater postoperative stone clearance. Protocolised TA may provide a brief intraoperative motion-control option with pre-oxygenation, continuous anaesthetic monitoring, and individualised termination.
