The mean (standard deviation) active lithotripsy efficiency was 27.8 (8.9), 26.6 (8.0), and 34.3 (10.0) mm3/min with RMV, STVV, and TA, respectively (P < 0.001). TA increased adjusted efficiency by 5.9 mm3/min vs RMV (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.2-9.6 mm3/min) and 6.8 mm3/min vs STVV (95% CI 3.3-10.2 mm3/min). The median active lithotripsy time was 27.5, 26.5, and 22.0 min (P = 0.001); total operative time was 50.0, 50.0, and 43.0 min (P = 0.002); and surgeon-rated targeting stability scores were 7.0, 7.0, and 9.0 (P < 0.001), respectively. Postoperative Day 1/1-month stone-free rates were 88%/92%, 80%/96%, and 88%/90%, respectively, with no significant between-group differences. The median (interquartile range) achieved apnoea duration was 5.0 (4.5-6.8) min; 46/50 resumed ventilation before the 9-min maximum, most commonly for heart-rate decline/bradycardia (n = 27) or blood-pressure decline/hypotension (n = 20). No patient had a peripheral oxygen saturation <90% or a Clavien-Dindo Grade ≥III complication; transient hypercapnia and respiratory acidosis improved after ventilation resumed.

Conclusion

Transient apnoea improved lithotripsy efficiency and shortened operative time compared with RMV and STVV, with higher surgeon-rated targeting stability. The benefit was primarily intraoperative, without evidence of greater postoperative stone clearance. Protocolised TA may provide a brief intraoperative motion-control option with pre-oxygenation, continuous anaesthetic monitoring, and individualised termination.

title: A Familial Case of Thauvin-Robinet-Faivre Syndrome (TROFAS), Presenting With Postaxial Polydactyly and Upper Lip Vascular Malformation.
abstract: Thauvin-Robinet-Faivre syndrome (TROFAS, OMIM #617107) is a recently identified autosomal recessive disorder characterised by syndromic overgrowth, facial dysmorphism, mild intellectual disability, variable congenital anomalies, and occasional tumour occurrence. TROFAS results from homozygous or compound heterozygous variants in the FIBP gene, encoding the intracellular binding protein for acidic fibroblast growth factor. This protein plays a role in the fibroblast growth factor (FGF) signalling pathway, which is involved in cell proliferation and contributes to the development of several structures, such as the nervous system, optic vesicles, and blood vessels. Prior to the present report, TROFAS has been described in 10 patients from seven families, four of which are of Turkish origin. We report two additional Turkish siblings from a previously unreported family harbouring the recurrent homozygous c.412-3_415dupCAGTTTG likely pathogenic variant in FIBP. Both presented with typical TROFAS features; however, the male sibling exhibited a more severe neurodevelopmental profile and additional malformations, including postaxial polydactyly and upper lip vascular malformation, which, to our knowledge, have not previously been reported in association with TROFAS. A detailed clinical characterisation of these two new cases contributes to a more comprehensive delineation of the syndrome, adding potentially novel phenotypic features requiring confirmation in additional patients.

title: PRAME Immunohistochemistry and Molecular Profiling in Undifferentiated Cutaneous Pleomorphic Neoplasms: A Case Series of 8 Tumors.
abstract: Background Undifferentiated cutaneous pleomorphic neoplasms are diagnostically challenging, as histopathology and immunohistochemistry often fail to identify undifferentiated melanoma in lesions that instead remain classified provisionally as atypical fibroxanthoma (AFX) or pleomorphic dermal sarcoma (PDS). Given the prognostic and therapeutic implications of melanoma, additional ancillary tools may be helpful in selected cases. Methods We studied eight patients with undifferentiated pleomorphic neoplasms using molecular profiling and PRAME immunohistochemistry, correlating findings with clinical behavior. Results Molecular findings varied across the cohort. Two tumors harbored NRAS hotspot mutations and were associated with aggressive clinical courses. In one patient, the tumor showed focal melanoma in situ associated with an undifferentiated intradermal tumor harboring NF1, TERT, and TP53 variants. The remaining tumors lacked melanoma-associated hotspot mutations. Diffuse PRAME expression was seen in three patients with an established diagnosis of melanoma and three patients with AFX/PDS. Two patients with AFX/PDS were negative for PRAME expression. Conclusions Molecular profiling may provide supportive diagnostic evidence for melanoma lineage in a subset of undifferentiated cutaneous pleomorphic neoplasms when interpreted in conjunction with morphology, immunohistochemistry, and clinical findings. In contrast, diffuse PRAME expression was observed in a nonspecific fashion both in cases with melanoma driver mutations and molecularly nonspecific cases in this cohort, limiting its utility as a standalone screening test for triaging molecular analysis.

title: Ηip dysplasia in children with spina bifida after prenatal surgical closure.
abstract: Aim To determine the prevalence of neonatal hip dysplasia in children with spina bifida after prenatal surgical closure and examine its association with functional level and preterm birth. Method We conducted a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected standardized registry data from a tertiary specialized centre providing comprehensive spina bifida diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up. Standardized hip ultrasound according to the Graf method was performed as part of a protocolized clinical pathway after prenatal surgery, within the first week of life corrected for preterm birth. The primary outcome was the prevalence of hip dysplasia at the initial ultrasound. Associations between hip status, functional level, and gestational age were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation. Results A total of 212 children (101 males, 111 females) underwent prenatal surgical closure between 1st January 2011 and 30th August 2022; 168 children (336 hips) had available neonatal ultrasound data and were included in the analysis. Preterm birth was present in 138 (82%) of 168 children, including 99 (59%) born late preterm, 35 (21%) born very preterm, and four (2%) born extremely preterm. At the initial ultrasound, 286 (85%) of 336 hips were mature, 33 (9.8%) were immature, and 17 (5.1%) were dysplastic. Worse hip status was weakly associated with a higher functional level (r = -0.243; p < 0.001), whereas no significant association was found between hip dysplasia and preterm birth (p = 0.080). Interpretation The prevalence of neonatal hip dysplasia in children with spina bifida after prenatal surgical closure was within the range reported for the general population.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Ultrasound for Sarcopenia Assessment: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Background Muscle ultrasound offers a portable, non-invasive, and cost-effective option for sarcopenia assessment, but operator dependency limits its standardization. Artificial intelligence (AI) may help automate and improve ultrasound-based muscle evaluation. This scoping review aims to map the current landscape of AI-assisted ultrasound for sarcopenia assessment, including research trends, methods, clinical uses and performance, and to suggest future work. Methods Following Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines and the PRISMA-ScR checklist, we searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, CINAHL, ProQuest, CNKI, WanFang Data, Yiigle, VIP, and Sinomed up to July 25, 2026. Two researchers independently selected studies and extracted data. Results Thirty studies were included. This field is developing rapidly, with 76.7% of studies published in the last 3 years, primarily from Spain and China. Model development and validation studies (43.3%) were most common. U-Net and its variants were the predominant AI architectures, mainly for image segmentation. B-mode ultrasound with high-frequency linear probes was frequently used. The rectus femoris was the most assessed muscle for sarcopenia (73.3%). AI-integrated models for sarcopenia diagnosis achieved AUCs of 0.640-0.950. Reported Dice coefficients for muscle segmentation ranged from 0.73 to 0.99. In-house datasets were used in 66.7% of the studies, and global classification labels were the most frequent annotation strategy (46.7%). Conclusions AI-assisted ultrasound shows potential for objective and scalable sarcopenia assessment but remains early-stage. Operator dependency in image acquisition has not been fully resolved. Further investigation should determine the added value of integrating multimodal imaging, combining diverse AI techniques, and evaluating multiple muscle groups. Future efforts should deepen image-processing strategies to extract clinically relevant features and facilitate standardized, scalable implementation in clinical practice.

title: Benign Proliferative Nodules in a Giant Congenital Melanocytic Nevus: Diagnostic Challenge and Management.
abstract: Congenital melanocytic nevi are cutaneous malformations present at birth, resulting from a benign proliferation of melanocytes. Although generally benign, they can have significant psychological impacts and carry a non-negligible risk of progression to malignant melanoma. We report a case of a giant congenital melanocytic nevus associated with a perianal mass in an infant, two and half-month-old infant, with no notable medical history, born at term. He was referred for a pigmented perianal swelling located on a large hyperpigmented plaque covering the lower back, buttocks, perineum, external genitalia, and the upper third of the thighs, consistent with a giant nevus. Multiple pigmented maculopapular satellite lesions were present, extending from the scalp to the soles of the feet. All lesions had been present since birth. The general examination was unremarkable. Doppler ultrasound revealed a well-defined, homogeneous, hypoechoic subcutaneous lesion with low vascularity, and skin biopsy confirmed a benign proliferative nodule. The proposed management included surgical excision, neurological and growth development follow-up, and psychosocial support for the infant and the parents. Six months after surgery, follow-up showed no evidence of recurrence, with the infant demonstrating normal neurological function and appropriate growth and developmental progress. This case highlights the importance of an accurate clinical and histological diagnosis and a multidisciplinary approach to management. It contributes to the limited local data from Madagascar and may contribute to the understanding of potential complications and their management.

title: Disseminated Tuberculosis With Ocular Involvement After 12 Years of Anti-TNF- α Therapy.
abstract: Background Ocular tuberculosis (TB) is an uncommon yet potentially vision-threatening manifestation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis , particularly difficult to diagnose in immunocompromised individuals. The increasing use of anti-tumor necrosis factor- α (anti-TNF- α ) agents has markedly heightened the risk of TB reactivation, often with disseminated or extrapulmonary involvement despite negative baseline screening. Case presentation We describe a 52-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis receiving long-term adalimumab and methotrexate who developed disseminated TB with pulmonary, splenic, and ocular involvement after 12 years of anti-TNF- α therapy. Baseline screening had shown a negative tuberculin skin test and an indeterminate interferon- γ release assay. She presented with constitutional and respiratory symptoms, whereas chest computed tomography demonstrated diffuse micronodular infiltrates consistent with miliary TB. Microbiological confirmation was obtained via bronchoalveolar lavage. Ophthalmologic evaluation revealed bilateral choroidal granulomas with subretinal edema, leading to a diagnosis of ocular TB. Standard antitubercular therapy (ATT) was initiated but required modification due to drug-induced liver injury. Adjunctive systemic corticosteroids were introduced after antimicrobial therapy and gradually tapered. The patient achieved progressive clinical, radiological, and ophthalmologic improvement, with gradual regression of choroidal lesions. Discussion This case underscores the persistent long-term risk of TB reactivation during prolonged anti-TNF- α therapy and highlights the limitations of current screening strategies in immunosuppressed patients. Ocular TB requires integration of systemic, clinical, and imaging findings; in this patient, microbiologically confirmed disseminated TB together with characteristic bilateral choroidal granulomas supported a definitive diagnosis. Management relies on prompt ATT, discontinuation of immunosuppression, and judicious use of adjunctive corticosteroids. Long-term follow-up is essential given the risk of persistent lesions and late recurrence. Reintroduction of biologic therapy may be feasible in selected cases but requires careful risk stratification. Ocular tuberculosis (TB) is an uncommon yet potentially vision-threatening manifestation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, particularly difficult to diagnose in immunocompromised individuals. The increasing use of anti-tumor necrosis factor-α (anti-TNF-α) agents has markedly heightened the risk of TB reactivation, often with disseminated or extrapulmonary involvement despite negative baseline screening.

We describe a 52-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis receiving long-term adalimumab and methotrexate who developed disseminated TB with pulmonary, splenic, and ocular involvement after 12 years of anti-TNF-α therapy. Baseline screening had shown a negative tuberculin skin test and an indeterminate interferon-γ release assay. She presented with constitutional and respiratory symptoms, whereas chest computed tomography demonstrated diffuse micronodular infiltrates consistent with miliary TB. Microbiological confirmation was obtained via bronchoalveolar lavage. Ophthalmologic evaluation revealed bilateral choroidal granulomas with subretinal edema, leading to a diagnosis of ocular TB. Standard antitubercular therapy (ATT) was initiated but required modification due to drug-induced liver injury. Adjunctive systemic corticosteroids were introduced after antimicrobial therapy and gradually tapered. The patient achieved progressive clinical, radiological, and ophthalmologic improvement, with gradual regression of choroidal lesions.

This case underscores the persistent long-term risk of TB reactivation during prolonged anti-TNF-α therapy and highlights the limitations of current screening strategies in immunosuppressed patients. Management relies on prompt ATT, discontinuation of immunosuppression, and judicious use of adjunctive corticosteroids. Long-term follow-up is essential given the risk of persistent lesions and late recurrence. Reintroduction of biologic therapy may be feasible in selected cases but requires careful risk stratification.

TB should remain a diagnostic consideration in patients receiving biologic therapy who develop compatible systemic or ocular manifestations, even after long-term treatment and negative baseline screening. title: Recognizing Odontogenic Maxillary Sinusitis in the ENT Clinic: Four CT Findings That Should Prompt Dental Evaluation.
abstract: Objective: This retrospective cohort study evaluated the proportion of maxillary sinuses with radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution among patients with imaging-confirmed acute or chronic maxillary sinusitis presenting to a single academic ENT clinic over one year. Sixty-five CT scans (84 sinuses) underwent multidisciplinary review for prespecified radiographic features. By highlighting imaging findings indicative of dental origin this study aims to improve recognition of possible odontogenic disease and appropriate multidisciplinary evaluation. Methods: Sixty-five patients were evaluated. Inclusion criteria required a visit diagnosis of chronic maxillary sinusitis (ICD10 J32.0) or acute maxillary sinusitis (ICD10 J01.00, J01.01), and a sinus CT within the preceding year. Each scan underwent multidisciplinary review by an oral and maxillofacial radiologist, an otolaryngologist, an otolaryngology resident, and a medical student. Scans were evaluated for maxillary sinus floor mucosal thickening and radiographic features suggestive of an odontogenic contribution, including periapical pathology, oroantral communication, large dental restorations, and widened periodontal ligament (PDL) space. Dental referral recommendations were based on multidisciplinary consensus from CT findings alone. Data were summarized using descriptive statistics. Results: Radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution were identified in 50/84 (59.52%) affected maxillary sinuses from 40 patients. Among these 50 sinuses, 17 (34%) showed widened PDL space, 15 (30%) showed oroantral communication, 28 (56%) showed periapical pathology, and 9 (18%) showed large dental restorations. There was consensus among the multidisciplinary team that in retrospect, among the 40 patients with OS, 38 required dental referrals. Conclusion: Radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution indicated a higher single-center cohort prevalence than expected based on population-level prevalence reports. The findings support deliberate review of the maxillary dentition on sinus CT, with this study outlining the key imaging features for odontogenic sinusitis.

title: MTL-LymphNet: A Lightweight Multi-Task Learning Framework for Simultaneous Lymph Node Segmentation and Metastasis Classification in Thyroid Cancer Ultrasound.
abstract: Ultrasound assessment of cervical lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma is crucial but suffers from inter-observer variability. Existing deep learning solutions typically use separate single-task pipelines, resulting in parameter redundancy. We propose MTL-LymphNet, a lightweight, backbone-agnostic multi-task learning framework that simultaneously segments lymph nodes and classifies metastasis within a single forward pass, evaluated across 3 backbones and 4 loss weighting strategies. On 338 images from 2 independent clinical centers, MTL-LymphNet achieved an internal cross-validation Dice coefficient of 0.891 ± 0.022 and AUC of 0.948 ± 0.027. Bidirectional external validation revealed substantial domain shift, with cross-center Dice of 0.865 and 0.779, and AUC of 0.733 and 0.830. The multi-task configuration offered a favorable efficiency-performance trade-off (∆Dice = Δ, -0.014, P < .0001) for 40% fewer parameters than separate models. No backbone or weighting strategy consistently dominated, and calibration degraded substantially under domain shift (ECE: 0.049 internally vs 0.178-0.304 externally), requiring center-specific recalibration before clinical use. To our knowledge, this is the first MTL framework for cervical lymph node analysis with bidirectional multi-center validation and systematic ablation. With a compact size of 22.6 to 29.1 MB and CPU inference of 81 to 131 ms, MTL-LymphNet demonstrates technical feasibility as a CAD tool warranting prospective validation.

title: Cardiac diagnostic modalities in polycythemia vera: A narrative review.
abstract: Polycythemia vera is a chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm in which erythrocytosis, Janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription activation, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and abnormal blood-cell activation converge to increase cardiovascular risk. This narrative review examines how electrocardiography, echocardiography, coronary angiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and right-heart catheterization contribute to recognition and characterization of cardiac involvement in polycythemia vera. Reported abnormalities include QT and P-wave changes, atrial arrhythmias, acute coronary syndromes, subclinical biventricular dysfunction, pulmonary hypertension, intracardiac thrombosis, and hypertrophic remodeling. Large observational datasets in myeloproliferative neoplasms also exhibit clinically important burdens of myocardial infarction, heart-failure hospitalization, bleeding, and echocardiographic pulmonary hypertension, although polycythemia vera-specific estimates remain limited. Baseline cardiovascular testing is increasingly relevant before novel therapies and trial enrollment; however, an abnormal test should prompt confirmation, reversible-cause assessment, and protocol-specific review rather than be treated as a universal contraindication. Hematocrit control and low-dose aspirin reduce thrombotic events, while evidence that cytoreductive therapy reverses electrocardiography or imaging abnormalities remains sparse. A symptom- and risk-directed diagnostic approach, integrated with hematology and cardiology assessment, is therefore more defensible than routine universal cardiac screening.

title: An Integrated Approach to MSI-High Colorectal Cancer Therapy in a Young Patient: A Clinical Case.
abstract: BACKGROUND Colorectal cancer (CRC) is extremely rare in adolescents and often presents with advanced disease because of nonspecific symptoms. Deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) and microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) are important biomarkers that influence prognosis, treatment selection, and the need for genetic evaluation. We report the case of an adolescent with MSI-H-associated CRC presenting with acute intestinal obstruction. CASE REPORT A 16-year-old male initially underwent appendectomy for presumed acute appendicitis. Persistent postoperative bowel obstruction prompted computed tomography (CT), revealing a descending colon tumor requiring emergency Hartmann's procedure. Histopathology demonstrated mucinous adenocarcinoma, pT4N0M0, with vascular invasion. Immunohistochemistry showed loss of MSH2/MSH6 expression with retained MLH1/PMS2, indicating dMMR and findings highly suggestive of Lynch syndrome, although germline testing was unavailable. Molecular analysis identified a KRAS mutation without NRAS alterations. Given his multiple high-risk features, including T4 disease, bowel obstruction, vascular invasion, mucinous histology, and very young age, he received 12 cycles of adjuvant FOLFOX chemotherapy. Treatment was well tolerated, and he remains disease-free more than 5 years after completion of therapy. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of adolescent CRC and the need to consider colorectal malignancy in young patients with persistent or atypical abdominal symptoms. Routine MMR/MSI testing and comprehensive molecular profiling are essential in young-onset CRC to identify patients who may have hereditary cancer syndromes and require genetic counseling. Although limited to a single case, this report underscores the importance of multidisciplinary decision-making and individualized treatment based on clinicopathological and molecular characteristics, which may contribute to favorable long-term outcomes.

title: Artificial intelligence in ophthalmic optical coherence tomography angiography: a bibliometric analysis.
abstract: Aim To analyze research landscapes, hotspots, and trends in artificial intelligence (AI) applied to ophthalmic optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) from 2015 to 2024, aiming to reveal global collaborations and guide future research. Methods We retrieved publications from Web of Science Core Collection using AI and OCTA-related search terms. After screening, 237 articles were analyzed with CiteSpace (version 6.3.R1) for co-citation, collaboration, and keyword burst analysis. Results Annual publications grew rapidly since 2017. China (94 publications) and the US (86 publications) were the most productive and influential countries. Research focused on: deep learning algorithms and vessel segmentation, ocular disease diagnosis including diabetic retinopathy and glaucoma, and automated vascular quantification and multimodal imaging. Key limitations included small sample sizes and limited algorithm generalizability. Conclusion The integration of AI with OCTA has significantly advanced the automation and precise quantitative analysis of ophthalmic vascular imaging, demonstrating substantial potential for diagnosing various retinal and choroidal diseases. Future efforts should focus on developing more robust and interpretable AI models, conducting large-scale, multi-center clinical validation, and establishing standardized imaging and analysis protocols to ultimately realize the widespread adoption of AI-OCTA technology in routine clinical practice.
originalAbstract:
Aim

To analyze research landscapes, hotspots, and trends in artificial intelligence (AI) applied to ophthalmic optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) from 2015 to 2024, aiming to reveal global collaborations and guide future research.

Methods

We retrieved publications from Web of Science Core Collection using AI and OCTA-related search terms. After screening, 237 articles were analyzed with CiteSpace (version 6.3.R1) for co-citation, collaboration, and keyword burst analysis.

Results

Annual publications grew rapidly since 2017. China (94 publications) and the US (86 publications) were the most productive and influential countries. Research focused on: deep learning algorithms and vessel segmentation, ocular disease diagnosis including diabetic retinopathy and glaucoma, and automated vascular quantification and multimodal imaging. Key limitations included small sample sizes and limited algorithm generalizability.

Conclusion

The integration of AI with OCTA has significantly advanced the automation and precise quantitative analysis of ophthalmic vascular imaging, demonstrating substantial potential for diagnosing various retinal and choroidal diseases. Future efforts should focus on developing more robust and interpretable AI models, conducting large-scale, multi-center clinical validation, and establishing standardized imaging and analysis protocols to ultimately realize the widespread adoption of AI-OCTA technology in routine clinical practice.

title: Deep learning integrated clinical-radiomics model for prognostic prediction in locally advanced cervical cancer through 18 F-FDG PET/CT and MRI combination
abstract: Abstract Background Precise pretreatment risk stratification is critical for guiding treatment intensification and personalized follow‑up in patients with locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) after concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT). This study developed and validated a deep learning integrated clinical-radiomics model for prognosis prediction in patients with LACC treated with CCRT, using dual-modal pretreatment imaging from 18 F-FDG PET/CT and contrast-enhanced MRI. Methods We retrospectively collected 346 patients (276 for training and 70 for testing) with LACC between June 2016 and October 2021. Radiomics and deep learning signatures were extracted from PET/CT and MRI. These signatures were integrated with the clinicopathological factors into a nomogram for clinical applications. Models were constructed using eleven machine learning algorithms, and a clinical-radiomics-deep learning model (CRDLM) was developed. The evaluation of the model’s performance was conducted through the metrics of the area under the curve (AUC). Results The CRDLM demonstrated superior predictive performance (AUCs of 0.998 (95% CI: 1.00–1.00) for training cohort and 0.901 (95% CI: 0.83–0.97) for testing cohort), which is significantly superior to conventional clinical factors (FIGO stage and SCC-Ag, AUC = 0.605–0.658). In addition, the CRDLM which combined radiomics with deep learning significantly outperformed the radiomics‑only model (AUC = 0.793, p = 0.006). Sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of CRDLM reached 0.947, 0.725, and 0.786, respectively. Conclusions The CRDLM provides robust prediction of disease progression in LACC patients who received CCRT, which may facilitate personalized treatment strategies and improve clinical outcomes. Further validation in multicenter prospective studies is warranted.

title: Can Chest CT Differentiate Between Low-Risk and Higher Risk Congenital Lung Lesions in Infants?
abstract: Abstract Purpose To determine whether chest CT can differentiate low-risk congenital lung lesions (pulmonary sequestration and CPAM type 2) from higher-risk lesions (CPAM type 1 and pleuropulmonary blastoma [PPB]) and thereby support the selection of patients for conservative management. Methods In this retrospective study (2003–2024), we identified infants with congenital lung lesions who underwent chest CT and subsequent pathologic confirmation. Two pediatric radiologists independently reviewed the anonymized CT scans, blinded to clinical and pathologic data. Lesions with a systemic arterial supply or predominant hyperinflation were classified as low risk; those with a solitary cyst, a cyst > 2 cm, or a complex cyst without systemic supply were classified as higher risk. Diagnostic confidence was graded as low, moderate, or high. Pathologic diagnosis served as the reference standard, and Cohen’s kappa was used to assess interobserver agreement. Results Eighty-three children (52 male) were included. Low-risk lesions (n = 73) comprised CPAM type 2 with or without sequestration (n = 51), isolated sequestration (n = 18), and other benign lesions (n = 4). Higher-risk lesions (n = 10) included CPAM type 1 (n = 8) and type I PPB (n = 2). For moderate-to-high-confidence diagnoses, sensitivity was 100% for both radiologists; specificity was 89.2% and 93.1%; and the negative predictive value was 100%. Interobserver agreement was almost perfect (98.4%; κ = 0.95). Conclusion Chest CT enables reliable differentiation of higher-risk from low-risk congenital lung lesions and can guide the selection of candidates for conservative management.

title: Unintentional Weight Loss Preceding Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Case Report and Review of Possible Mechanisms
abstract: Abstract Background Unintentional weight loss is not a recognized presenting feature of multiple sclerosis (MS) and is more commonly associated with malignancy, chronic infection, endocrine disorders, gastrointestinal disease, or systemic inflammatory conditions. We report an unusual case in which marked involuntary weight loss preceded the diagnosis of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS). Case Presentation: A 37-year-old man presented with acute gait impairment and right lower-extremity weakness. Retrospective history revealed gradual unintentional weight loss from approximately 97 kg to 68 kg over nearly two years despite preserved appetite and the absence of gastrointestinal, infectious, endocrine, or constitutional symptoms. Extensive investigations, including laboratory testing, infectious screening, tumor markers, upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, abdominal ultrasonography, and chest imaging, failed to identify an alternative cause. Neurological examination demonstrated right lower-extremity weakness, generalized hyperreflexia, bilateral pyramidal signs, and an Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score of 4.0. Brain and cervical spinal cord magnetic resonance imaging revealed multiple typical demyelinating lesions fulfilling the 2017 McDonald criteria for MS. The patient received intravenous methylprednisolone followed by rituximab (1000 mg every 6 months). During four years of follow-up, the EDSS score improved from 4.0 to 1.0, MRI studies remained stable, and body weight gradually returned to two years before the start of the disease. Conclusion This case describes marked, unexplained weight loss preceding the diagnosis of RRMS, which resolved after treatment initiation and disease stabilization. Although causality cannot be established, the temporal association suggests that clinically significant weight loss may represent an uncommon and underrecognized manifestation of active MS. Further studies are needed to clarify the frequency and mechanisms of weight changes in MS.

title: Follicular Dendritic Cell Sarcoma Arising in the Aortopulmonary Window: A Case Report of Complete Resection Using Proximal Pulmonary Artery Control
abstract: Abstract Background: Follicular dendritic cell sarcoma is a rare malignant neoplasm, and its occurrence in the aortopulmonary window is exceptionally uncommon. Tumors in this location are technically challenging because of the limited operative space and their close relationship to the aortic arch, left pulmonary artery, left main bronchus, and left recurrent laryngeal nerve. We report a case of follicular dendritic cell sarcoma arising in the aortopulmonary window that was completely resected using a strategy for proximal pulmonary artery control. Case presentation: A 46-year-old man was referred to our institution after an abnormal mediastinal shadow was incidentally detected on chest radiography. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography showed a 48 × 29 mm well-circumscribed mass in the aortopulmonary window, broadly contacting the aorta, left pulmonary artery, and left main bronchus. Positron emission tomography showed moderate fluorodeoxyglucose uptake without distant metastasis. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration suggested a neuroendocrine tumor but did not establish a definitive diagnosis. Surgical resection was performed through median sternotomy combined with a left anterior second intercostal thoracotomy. Because direct exposure and encirclement of the tumor-adjacent left pulmonary artery were considered hazardous, proximal vascular control was established through the transverse pericardial sinus before tumor manipulation. Division of the ligamentum arteriosum increased pulmonary artery mobility and improved exposure of the operative field. The tumor was completely separated from the left pulmonary artery, aorta, left main bronchus, and recurrent laryngeal nerve without combined organ resection. Histopathological examination showed spindle-shaped tumor cells arranged in whorled and rosette-like patterns. Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CD21, CD23, D2-40, and somatostatin receptor 2, confirming follicular dendritic cell sarcoma. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remained free of recurrence 3 years after surgery. Conclusions: Complete resection of a tumor arising in the aortopulmonary window can be facilitated by secure proximal pulmonary artery control and mobilization of surrounding structures. These technical principles may also be useful for other tumors in this anatomically complex region when direct manipulation of the tumor-adjacent pulmonary artery is considered hazardous.

title: Association of intratumoral and peritumoral apparent diffusion coefficients with stromal tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte levels in primary triple-negative breast cancer: a retrospective 3-T MRI study
abstract: Abstract Background Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are associated with treatment response and prognosis in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but their assessment requires tissue sampling. We investigated whether routine pretreatment imaging findings, particularly intratumoral and peritumoral apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) measurements on 3-T breast MRI, were associated with stromal TIL levels and evaluated an exploratory MRI-based model. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 79 consecutive women with primary TNBC assessed between November 2016 and October 2023. High TIL status was defined as stromal TILs ≥ 10% in pretreatment biopsy specimens. Mammographic, ultrasonographic, MRI, and ¹⁸F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT findings were analyzed when available. A prespecified MRI-based logistic regression model included intratumoral ADC, peritumoral ADC, and MRI margin. Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis and internally validated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Associations with pathological complete response (pCR) were explored. Results High TIL status was present in 57 of 79 participants (72.2%). Among 76 participants with MRI, higher intratumoral ADC (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 6.96; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.47–19.67; p < 0.001) and lower peritumoral ADC (adjusted OR, 0.27; 95% CI, 0.11–0.66; p = 0.004) were independently associated with high TIL status. The exploratory MRI-based model had an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.934 (95% CI, 0.879–0.989) and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.914. Intratumoral ADC alone had an AUC of 0.856 (95% CI, 0.768–0.944). The associations remained consistent after adjustment for the MRI system and in the analysis restricted to the predominant Ingenia 3.0T system. In exploratory analyses, pCR was more frequent in participants with high versus low TIL status (58.1% vs. 7.7%; p = 0.001) and in those with high versus low intratumoral ADC (57.1% vs. 8.3%; p = 0.003). Conclusions Routine intratumoral and peritumoral ADC measurements were associated with high stromal TIL status in this single-center TNBC cohort. The exploratory MRI-based model showed good discrimination after bootstrap correction. External multicenter evaluation is required before clinical use.

title: Edematous dermatomyositis as a rare cause of isolated bilateral arm swelling in a patient with urothelial carcinoma: case report and literature review
abstract: Abstract Background Edematous dermatomyositis (DM) is a rare manifestation of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy and may initially resemble vascular causes of upper-limb swelling. Early recognition is clinically important because severe cases require prompt immunosuppressive treatment and because adult-onset DM, particularly in the presence of anti-transcription intermediary factor 1-gamma (anti-TIF1-γ) antibodies, has a close association with malignancy. Case presentation: An 86-year-old Caucasian woman with recently treated high-grade, muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of the bladder presented with a 2.5-week history of progressive, severe bilateral upper-extremity edema, proximal muscle weakness, and a violaceous eruption involving the periorbital region, face, anterior neck, and upper chest, accompanied by Gottron papules. Duplex ultrasonography excluded upper-extremity deep vein thrombosis and superficial venous thrombosis. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography of the chest and abdomen excluded central venous obstruction, thoracic or abdominal tumor recurrence, and metastasis. Electromyography and bilateral shoulder/upper-arm magnetic resonance imaging were compatible with active myositis, and myositis serology was positive for anti-TIF1-γ antibodies. During hospitalization, muscle weakness and dysphagia progressed rapidly. After insufficient clinical response to prednisolone and intravenous immunoglobulin, rituximab was administered as salvage therapy. Despite treatment, weakness and dysphagia progressed, and the patient died 6 weeks after admission. Conclusions Edematous dermatomyositis should be considered in the differential diagnosis of otherwise unexplained bilateral upper-limb edema after upper-extremity venous thrombosis and superior vena cava syndrome have been excluded, particularly in the presence of proximal muscle weakness, dysphagia, or dermatomyositis-specific cutaneous findings. The diagnosis of DM should prompt structured oncologic reassessment and surveillance, especially in patients with anti-TIF1-γ positivity or recent malignancy.

title: Interactive Lesion Segmentation in Whole-Body PET/CT and Longitudinal CT: The autoPET/CT-IV Challenge
abstract: Abstract Deep learning enables automated tumour segmentation in whole-body positron emission tomography and computed tomography, but robustness remains limited by heterogeneous tracer uptake, anatomical variability, and inter-center differences. We report the fourth autoPET challenge, which evaluated interactive lesion segmentation using incremental simulated user prompts and longitudinal lesion segmentation from paired baseline and follow-up scans. In the interactive task (Task 1, ~ 30,000 training and ~ 3,000 test lesions), submitted methods improved with additional user input and achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.74 at the final interaction step, with performance remaining robust across tracers and centers. Longitudinal segmentation (Task 2, ~ 7,500 training and ~ 4,500 test lesions) was substantially more challenging, with a best mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.38. Here, we show that interactive segmentation can combine automated inference with iterative expert input while maintaining performance across heterogeneous imaging domains, whereas longitudinal lesion prediction remains limited by temporal and anatomical variability.

title: Halo-Femoral Traction and Staged Surgical Correction for Severe Rigid Adult Scoliosis: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Surgical correction of severe rigid adult spinal deformities (ASD) with Cobb angles exceeding 100° is highly challenging due to risks of neurological injury and poor spinal flexibility. Preoperative halo-femoral traction enhances spinal compliance, facilitating safer staged corrective surgery. Few cases of this procedure for curvatures approaching 150° have been reported. Case Presentation: A 24-year-old female presented with severe right thigh and knee pain secondary to a 148° rigid thoracolumbar kyphoscoliosis. Initial imaging revealed minimal flexibility (bend correction to 94°) without neural compromise. The patient underwent continuous halo-femoral traction for several weeks to improve spinal flexibility, The patient was managed via a sequential two-step protocol: initially, under anesthesia, halo and femoral pins were placed to apply continuous traction for maximizing spinal flexibility. Subsequently, the patient underwent definitive single-stage posterior spinal instrumentation and deformity correction. Intraoperative neuromonitoring was utilized throughout to ensure neurological safety. Continuous multi-modal intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM), including somatosensory-evoked potentials (SSEPs) and motor-evoked potentials (MEPs), was utilized throughout all two surgical stages. No significant or sustained changes in SSEP or MEP signals were observed during the corrective maneuvers, supporting the early detection of potential neurological compromise and guiding safe deformity correction. Conclusion: Postoperatively, the patient achieved significant correction with a final Cobb angle of approximately 50°, accompanied by marked pain relief, improved truncal balance, and enhanced functional status as measured by clinical video-based clinical observation of gait. Radiographs at 6 weeks and subsequent follow-ups demonstrated stable fusion and sustained alignment. No neurological deficits or major complications were observed. This case illustrates the feasibility of utilizing prolonged halo-femoral traction combined with a carefully planned surgical algorithm in the management of extreme rigid adult scoliosis. The technical and strategic framework provided herein may inform clinical practice guidelines and warrants further investigation in larger cohorts.

title: Pericardial Effusion Presenting as Isolated Right Upper Quadrant Pain with Deranged Liver Enzymes a Diagnostic Pitfall in the Emergency Department a Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Pericardial effusion typically presents with chest pain, dyspnoea, and positional discomfort. Presentation with isolated abdominal pain in the absence of cardiopulmonary symptoms is rare and closely mimics acute hepatobiliary pathology. Recognition is critical, since unrecognised pericardial effusion may progress to life-threatening cardiac tamponade. Case Presentation A 43-year-old black African woman with virologically suppressed human immunodeficiency virus infection (HIV), ulcerative colitis, and a history of previously treated latent tuberculosis (TB) infection presented to the emergency department with a one-day history of abdominal pain radiating to the flanks and epigastrium. Right upper quadrant tenderness on examination and elevated liver enzymes upon further investigation prompted a provisional diagnosis of cholecystitis. A subsequent chest radiograph showed a globular cardiac silhouette and bedside echocardiography confirmed a large pericardial effusion. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated an effusion with features of right cardiac impairment, hepatic congestion and pericholecystic fluid, with no evidence of acute cholecystitis. Pericardiocentesis yielded haemoserous fluid, with resolution of symptoms and improvement in liver enzymes. The effusion re-accumulated within 5 days, with right ventricular diastolic collapse and this was surgically managed. The rapid recurrence raised suspicion of a potential inflammatory aetiology; however, the definitive aetiology remains unclear. Conclusions Pericardial effusion should be considered in patients with undifferentiated abdominal pain and liver enzyme derangement, even in the absence of typical cardiac symptoms or Beck’s triad. This case highlights the potential for cardiac pathology to mimic acute hepatobiliary disease and emphasises the importance of maintaining a broad differential diagnosis in atypical abdominal presentations.

title: ABC versus C-Rad Technology for Intrafraction Displacement and Dosimetric Impact in Breast Cancer Radiotherapy with Breath-Hold
abstract: Abstract Purpose To compare treatment time, intrafraction errors, and dosimetric effects between active breathing control (ABC) and C-Rad optical surface monitoring in postoperative breast cancer radiotherapy. Methods Thirty patients with postoperative breast cancer were enrolled, including 15 patients in the ABC group and 15 in the C-Rad group. All patients were immobilized using a KoalaRedi arm support combined with a negative-pressure vacuum cushion and received breath-hold radiotherapy. Treatment time was recorded for each fraction. Intrafraction errors in the X, Y, and Z directions were determined from cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans acquired immediately after treatment. The Mann–Whitney U test was used for intergroup comparisons. Spearman’s rank correlation analysis was performed to assess the relationship between treatment time and intrafraction errors. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to determine the optimal treatment-time threshold for predicting a Z-direction error > 2 mm. Dosimetric simulations were performed using the maximum registration error for each patient to compare the planned dose distribution with the dose distribution after introduction of the corresponding error, with particular attention to doses to the heart, lungs, and target doses. Results Median treatment time was significantly shorter in the C-Rad group than in the ABC group (7.44 [6.50–8.07] min vs. 7.99 [7.23–8.51] min, P < 0.001). No significant intergroup differences were observed in X- or Y-direction errors; however, Z-direction errors were significantly larger in the C-Rad group (0.146 [0.06–0.21] cm vs. 0.113 [0.05–0.15] cm, P < 0.001). In the C-Rad group, Z-direction error was positively correlated with treatment time (r = 0.167, P = 0.006). A treatment time > 10.93 min predicted a Z-direction error > 2 mm (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.605; sensitivity, 86.3%; and specificity, 31.9%). Dosimetric simulation based on each patient’s maximum intrafraction error showed that, in the ABC group, the maximum error resulted in a mean reduction of 2.32% in planning target volume (PTV) D95 relative to the planned value (median, − 1.13%; P = 0.002), whereas changes in heart Dmean, ipsilateral lung V20, and mean lung dose were not statistically significant (all P > 0.05). In the C-Rad group, PTV D95 decreased by a mean of 3.80% (median, − 2.90%; P = 0.006), with no significant changes in the other dosimetric parameters. Conclusion The C-Rad technique resulted in significantly shorter single-fraction treatment times than ABC (7.44 vs. 7.99 min). However, although no significant intergroup differences were observed in lateral (X) or longitudinal (Y) errors, the vertical (Z) error was significantly larger in the C-Rad group (median, 0.13 [0.06–0.21] cm vs. 0.09 [0.05–0.15] cm, P < 0.001) and increased with longer treatment times. The threshold for predicting a Z-direction error > 2 mm was 10.93 min. Under maximum intrafraction error conditions, both techniques resulted in small reductions in target coverage (PTV D95: −2.32% for ABC and − 3.80% for C-Rad), without significant changes in doses to organs at risk.

The threshold for predicting a Z-direction error > 2 mm was 10.93 min. Under maximum intrafraction error conditions, both techniques resulted in small reductions in target coverage (PTV D95: −2.32% for ABC and − 3.80% for C-Rad), without significant changes in doses to organs at risk.

title: Epilepsy as an Initial Presentation of Superficial Siderosis of the Central Nervous System:A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Superficial siderosis of the central nervous system (SSCNS) is a rare neurological disorder resulting from chronic subarachnoid haemorrhage. Its classical clinical features comprise sensorineural hearing loss, cerebellar ataxia and pyramidal tract dysfunction. However, epilepsy as an initial presentation remains uncommon and insufficiently characterized. Case Presentation: We describe a 34-year-old male with a remote history of right brachial plexus injury, who presented with recurrent epileptic seizures as the predominant early symptom, followed by progressive hearing loss and gait instability. Neuroimaging demonstrated characteristic haemosiderin deposition on T2*-weighted and susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) sequences.Transient, seizure-related subcortical and periventricular restricted diffusion on diffusion-weighted imaging resolved completely within one month. Anti-epileptic medication achieved partial seizure control, but the patient’s neurological deficits exhibited gradual progression. Conclusion Epilepsy may represent an uncommon initial presentation of SSCNS. Targeted MRI sequences facilitate diagnosis. SSCNS should be considered in the differential diagnosis of patients with unexplained epilepsy,particularly those with a history of craniospinal trauma.

title: Single-port inflatable video-assisted mediastinoscopic transhiatal esophagectomy for esophageal cancer in a patient with left upper lobe destruction secondary to remote pulmonary tuberculosis: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Surgical resection is the cornerstone of curative treatment for resectable esophageal cancer. However, transthoracic esophagectomy (TTE) requires one-lung ventilation (OLV), which may be poorly tolerated by patients with severely impaired pulmonary function. Inflatable video-assisted mediastinoscopic transhiatal esophagectomy combined with laparoscopy (IVMTE), which avoids OLV, may offer an alternative surgical approach for these patients. Case presentation A 70-year-old man presented with a 1-month history of dysphagia. Endoscopic biopsy confirmed mid-thoracic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). He had a history of pulmonary tuberculosis with radiographic evidence of left upper lobe destruction. Pulmonary function testing revealed severe restrictive ventilatory impairment with impaired diffusing capacity, rendering him unable to tolerate transthoracic surgery. Following multidisciplinary evaluation, he underwent single-port inflatable video-assisted mediastinoscopic transhiatal esophagectomy combined with laparoscopy (SP-IVMTE), with an uneventful intraoperative course and no oxygen desaturation. Histopathology revealed a moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma invading the adventitia, with negative margins and no lymph node metastasis (pT3N0M0). The patient had an uneventful postoperative recovery and was discharged on postoperative day 14. The patient had an uneventful postoperative recovery. Follow-up CT scans through 24 months showed no evidence of recurrence or metastasis, and at the 29-month clinical follow-up, he remained asymptomatic with normal oral intake. Conclusions For patients with severely compromised pulmonary reserve who are unable to tolerate a transthoracic approach, IVMTE may provide a feasible individualized surgical option for curative treatment of esophageal cancer.

title: Sliding Amyand's hernia with acute appendicitis presenting as an incarcerated inguinoscrotal hernia: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background : Amyand's hernia, defined as the presence of the vermiform appendix within an inguinal hernia sac, is uncommon. Acute appendicitis within an Amyand's hernia is rarer, and a sliding variant in which the caecum contributes to the hernia sac adds further operative complexity. We report a case of sliding Amyand's hernia with acute appendicitis presenting as an incarcerated inguinoscrotal hernia. Case presentation: A 56-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with a one-day history of a painful, irreducible right inguinoscrotal swelling on a background of a three-year hernia. He was constipated but continued to pass flatus and had no fever or urinary symptoms. Examination showed a tender irreducible right inguinoscrotal hernia with a soft, non-tender abdomen and no peritonism. The white cell count was 19 × 10⁹/L and C-reactive protein was 142 mg/L. Plain abdominal radiography showed dilated small bowel loops. Computed tomography was difficult to arrange on an emergency basis. Although ultrasonography was available, it was not requested because the clinical diagnosis of an incarcerated inguinal hernia was sufficiently compelling to warrant operative management, and the anticipated findings were unlikely to alter the decision to proceed with surgery. At exploration, the caecum was found to form part of the wall of the hernia sac within the right hemiscrotum, with a grossly inflamed appendix and inflammatory fluid. There was no features of bowel ischaemia or gangrene. Appendicectomy and primary non-mesh tissue repair were performed. Histology confirmed acute appendicitis. The postoperative course was uncomplicated, and the patient was well at three-week follow-up. Conclusion: Sliding Amyand's hernia with acute appendicitis should be considered as a differential diagnosis in patients presenting with an incarcerated inguinoscrotal hernia and disproportionate inflammatory markers. Although the diagnosis is often established intraoperatively, awareness of this possibility may improve operative preparedness. Intraoperative assessment of appendiceal inflammation, contamination and the sliding caecal anatomy should guide appendiceal management and the choice of hernia repair. In this patient, appendicectomy with primary tissue repair was followed by an uncomplicated early recovery.

title: Salvage computed tomography-guided brachytherapy for patients with postoperative vaginal recurrence of endometrial cancer
abstract: Abstract Background This study retrospectively analyzed the treatment outcomes of computed tomography (CT)-guided brachytherapy (BT) for vaginal recurrence after endometrial cancer surgery. Methods Patients with vaginal recurrence after endometrial cancer surgery who underwent CT-guided BT between were retrospectively analyzed. The primary endpoint was local control (LC). Secondary endpoints included regional recurrence-free survival (RRFS), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and late toxicities. Results 50 patients were included. External beam radiotherapy (EBRT) with a median total dose of 50 Gy was administered to 30 patients. The median number of BT fractions was five for patients with superficial recurrence and three for those with visible recurrence, respectively. The median total dose delivered to the high-risk clinical target volume (HR-CTV) (equivalent dose in 2 Gy fractions; EQD2) was 70.5 Gy. The median follow-up period was 44.8 months. The 3-year LC, RRFS, DMFS, DFS, and OS rates were 85.6%, 82.9%, 65.1%, 46.0%, and 87.1%, respectively. In the univariate analysis, HR-CTV D90 was a significant prognostic factor for LC (p = 0.009). The 3-year LC rate was significantly higher in patients with HR-CTV D90 ≥ 67.3 Gy than in those with < 67.3 Gy (100% vs. 64.2%). In the multivariate analysis, tumor visibility and postoperative risk classification were significant prognostic factors for DMFS (p < 0.011 and p = 0.033, respectively). Conclusions CT-guided BT provides favorable local control in patients with vaginal recurrence after endometrial cancer surgery. However, distant metastases remain a major site of failure. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Construction of a Retinopathy of Prematurity Onset Prediction Model Using the Random Forest Machine Learning Algorithm
abstract: Abstract Objective: This study aimed to refine and validate a previously developed Random Forest prediction model for the onset of Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP), which was based on a machine learning approach. Methods: A retrospective study was conducted on 150 neonatal cases who met the inclusion criteria and underwent ROP screening at the Department of Neonatology, Wuzhou Workers' Hospital, Guangxi, China, between January 2024 and September 2024.1.Data on ROP-related risk factors and concurrent fundus screening results were collected by reviewing the electronic medical records (inpatient and follow-up outpatient) of the enrolled neonates.2.The top 15 risk factors identified from five distinct machine learning models were analyzed to identify the common risk factors among them.3.The Random Forest prediction model was validated. Results: 1.Nine common risk factors were identified from the top 15 factors across the five machine learning models: oxygen therapy, oxygen concentration, gestational age, birth weight, anemia of prematurity, neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS), necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), in vitro fertilization embryo transfer, and antibiotic use.2.Validation of the Random Forest model using the dataset from Wuzhou Workers' Hospital showed good performance on the validation set: AUC: 0.892, accuracy: 77.9%, specificity: 99.3%, sensitivity: 62.9%, precision: 89.9%. Conclusion: The Random Forest model, constructed using machine learning methods and incorporating predictive features such as oxygen therapy, oxygen concentration, gestational age, birth weight, anemia of prematurity, NRDS, NEC, in vitro fertilization embryo transfer, and antibiotic use, demonstrates good predictive value for ROP. This model holds potential for application in clinical screening of high-risk populations for retinopathy of prematurity.

title: Spatial Alignment of Parkinson’s Disease-Related Quantitative MRI Alterations with Dopaminergic Topography
abstract: Abstract Objective Parkinson’s disease (PD) is characterized by a degeneration of dopaminergic neurons not only in the nigrostriatal pathways, but also in subcortical and cortical structures. Given the widespread dopaminergic innervation, PD dopamine-related dysfunction may contribute to microstructural alterations beyond the primary site of pathology. Multiparametric mapping (MPM) enables quantification of tissue biophysical properties informing the brain’s microstructure. We hypothesized that PD-related MPM alterations would show distinct spatial associations with pre- and postsynaptic dopaminergic markers. Methods 31 patients with PD and 68 healthy controls underwent a 3T MRI. We used unthresholded MPM t-maps derived from group-difference analysis to assess spatial correlation with PET-derived maps of the dopamine transporter (DAT), [ 18 F]-fluoro-L-DOPA (FDOPA), and dopamine D1 and D2 receptors. Results Proton density alterations negatively correlated with DAT (rho = 0.355, p spatial = 0.0010) and FDOPA (rho = 0.168, p FDR = 0.0080) across whole-brain gray matter. Subcortically, MPM-dopaminergic associations were structure-specific, showing concordant, same-direction associations between FDOPA and D1. Cortically, associations were more consistent, predominantly negative and driven by DAT and FDOPA. Within cortical ROIs, presupplementary and supplementary motor areas showed the most robust associations, driven by proton density (preSMA: rho = 0.428 to 0.760; SMA: rho = 0.284 to 0.789, all p FDR < 0.0001). Interpretation: PD-related microstructural-dopaminergic associations were structure- and modality-specific. Subcortically, FDOPA and D1 consistently tracked microstructural alterations, potentially reflecting coupled degeneration of dopaminergic synthesis capacity and postsynaptic receptor density. Cortically, DAT and FDOPA most robustly tracked proton density-related alterations, potentially indicating distinct and mainly neuroinflammation-driven microstructural processes beyond the primary nigrostriatal network.

title: Transthoracic echocardiography for initial screening of single coronary artery anomaly: a case with multimodal imaging evaluation
abstract: Abstract Single coronary artery anomaly (SCA) is a rare congenital coronary malformation with only one aortic coronary ostium supplying the whole myocardium. Clinical outcomes mainly depend on the anatomical course of the aberrant vessel. We report a 73-year-old female presenting with intermittent precordial chest pain. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) revealed a dilated right coronary artery (RCA) with normal ostial location, non-visualization of the left coronary artery ostium, and diastolic low-resistance arterial flow signal within the interventricular septum along the expected left anterior descending artery (LAD) territory. Coronary computed-tomography angiography (CCTA) demonstrated right-dominant coronary circulation, absence of the native left coronary artery, and an abnormally extended posterior descending artery travelling into the anterior interventricular groove. Multimodal imaging highly suggested Lipton-Yamanaka type R-I SCA. The patient received conservative medical therapy for co-existing mild coronary atherosclerosis. This case underlines TTE as a valuable first-line screening tool for congenital coronary anomalies. Nevertheless, definitive subtyping requires CCTA or invasive coronary angiography.

title: [18F]NaF PET Radiomics and Coronary Calcium Score Progression: Associations Beyond Baseline Calcium Score and TBR
abstract: Abstract Background: [ 18 F]NaF positron emission tomography (PET) can quantify coronary calcification activity before coronary calcium score (CCS) progression, which is a surrogate measure of cardiovascular disease risk. It remains uncertain whether advanced PET quantification, including radiomics, improves prediction of CCS progression. Participants with type 2 diabetes underwent baseline [ 18 F]NaF PET/CT, baseline CCS and a follow-up CCS after 2 years. CCS progression was evaluated on a per-patient and a per-artery level. [ 18 F]NaF activity was evaluated using the TBR max , and radiomics features. Logistic regression models were used to determine the features most associated with CCS progression. Results: In total, 91 participants (median age [interquartile range]: 66 [60 – 70], 71.4% male) were examined. In total, 68 patients (74.7%) demonstrated CCS progression. Clinical variables and baseline CCS discriminated CCS progressors and non-progressors modestly (AUC 0.72, 95% CI 0.55–0.86). The TBR max demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.83, 95% CI 0.73–0.92), while multi-feature radiomics models achieved the highest discrimination performance (AUC 0.90, 95% CI 0.80–0.97). A total of 211 coronary arteries (58.0%) demonstrated CCS progression. The combined CCS and TBR max model discriminated CCS progressors and non-progressors modestly (AUC of 0.67, 95% CI 0.60–0.73), while the multi-feature radiomics demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.77, 95% CI: 0.70–0.84). Conclusions: [ 18 F]NaF PET radiomics improves prediction of CCS progression compared with baseline CCS, clinical features, and the TBR max .

title: Key performance indicators for organized risk stratified prostate cancer screening in Europe: first results from the PRAISE-U and EUCanScreen pilots and the Swedish organised prostate cancer testing programme
abstract: Abstract Background. Prostate cancer (PCa) is the most frequently diagnosed cancer in men in the European Union. Following the 2022 Council Recommendation to evaluate organised screening based on prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), PRAISE-U defined 21 harmonised key performance indicators (KPIs). We report their first empirical values from the five PRAISE-U pilots and, through a common survey, from EUCanScreen pilots and the Swedish organised prostate cancer testing (OPT) programme. Methods. In PRAISE-U, men aged 50–69 years at five pilot sites in Spain, Lithuania, Poland and Ireland were invited to risk-stratified screening comprising PSA testing, first-level risk stratification, MRI for intermediate or high risk and selective biopsy, with prospective capture in a central REDCap database. EUCanScreen pilots and the Swedish organised prostate cancer testing (OPT) programme reported the same KPIs through an online survey. Results. Twelve programmes reported KPI values. Across the five PRAISE-U pilots, participation ranged from 7.1% to 43.0%, PSA exceeded 3 ng/ml in 9.2–15.0%, and compliance was 76.4–96.0% for first-level risk assessment, 89.9–98.3% for MRI and 78.9–99.0% for biopsy. Detection ranged from 8 to 26 per 1,000 screened in PRAISE-U and from 4.3 to 28 across all programmes. ISUP grade 1 accounted for 20.3–81.4% of cancers, active-surveillance uptake for 14.8–100%, and mean time from PSA result to MRI for 19–114 days; external values fell broadly within the PRAISE-U ranges. Thirteen of 21 KPIs were fully reported by all five pilots, all describing the diagnostic pathway; retention and the three impact indicators were reported only by Sweden, which reported 19 of 21. Conclusions. Diagnostic-pathway KPIs were measurable under pilot conditions, whereas programme-level indicators required a defined target population or registry linkage. Sweden, the only population-based programme, reported retention and long-term impact, identifying the infrastructure needed before organised PCa screening can be monitored at scale.

title: Versajet® Hydrosurgery for Primary Axillary Hyperhidrosis with Osmidrosis: First Vietnamese Case Report with Histopathology
abstract: Abstract Background Conventional minimally invasive surgical techniques for axillary hyperhidrosis (e.g., cannula-assisted suction-curettage) carry risks of subdermal vascular plexus injury and flap necrosis (10–15%) [1] . The Versajet® Hydrosurgery System, employing the Venturi effect with high-pressure saline jet and continuous suction without thermal injury, represents a potential alternative [2,3] . Case presentation : A 33-year-old Vietnamese male (BMI 33.3 kg/m²) presented with 16-year history of bilateral primary axillary hyperhidrosis with osmidrosis (onset at age 18), HDSS 3 bilaterally, wet earwax phenotype (suggesting ABCC11 G-allele), DLQI 9/30, Park-Shin grade 3, meeting 5/6 Hornberger criteria [4] . Methods Surgery was performed on 23 April 2026 under Klein tumescent anesthesia (lidocaine 480 mg + epinephrine 1:1,000,000 + 500 mL 0.9% NaCl; 100 mL/axilla infiltration). The Versajet® II with a 45°/14 mm handpiece at power 6–8 (574 bar/8,330 psi) was used, consuming 500 mL 0.9% NaCl and 15 minutes of debridement per axilla through a 5-cm incision parallel to the axillary crease. Outcomes were assessed at 1 and 3 months using HDSS, DLQI, Park-Shin, and VSS, with paired pre-/post-excision histopathology. Results Total operative time was 100 minutes with blood loss < 30 mL and no intraoperative complications. VAS pain was 3/10 on days 1–3, resolving to 0/10 by day 10. At 3 months: HDSS 3→1, DLQI 9→1, Park-Shin 3→1, VSS 4/14, Clavien-Dindo grade I, patient satisfaction 5/5. Histopathology demonstrated 68.8–75.0% apocrine gland reduction and 32.3–45.5% eccrine gland reduction with preserved hair follicle architecture. Conclusion Hydrosurgery with the Versajet® System demonstrated high technical feasibility, significant clinical efficacy, and objective histopathological evidence of selective apocrine gland reduction while preserving the subdermal vascular plexus. Larger prospective cohort studies with long-term follow-up are warranted to standardize parameters and assess recurrence.

title: Enhanced Breast Cancer Classification by Integrating CNN and ViT on the CBIS-DDSM Mammography Dataset
abstract: Abstract Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of mortality among women worldwide, necessitating early and accurate diagnostic methods to improve patient outcomes. This study presents a novel hybrid approach for breast cancer classification by integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures, specifically applied to the publicly available CBIS-DDSM mammography dataset. The initial phase employs a CNN model, which excels in localized feature extraction through convolutional layers, to identify key patterns related to benign and malignant tumors. However, CNNs inherently focus on local features and may overlook broader contextual relationships within the image. To overcome this limitation, the study introduces a hybrid framework that combines CNN with the Vision Transformer model. ViT utilizes self-attention mechanisms to capture long-range dependencies and global context, complementing the localized feature extraction capability of CNNs. By integrating these two deep learning paradigms, the hybrid model effectively captures both fine-grained local details and overarching structural patterns within mammograms. Experimental results indicate that synergy results in an improved classification accuracy. The enhanced performance of the combined CNN-ViT model underscores the potential of hybrid deep learning strategies in medical image analysis. Moreover, this approach demonstrates robust generalization on the CBIS-DDSM dataset, which includes diverse mammographic cases. The findings not only provide a pathway to more reliable breast cancer detection tools but also contribute to reducing diagnostic burden and improving early intervention strategies.

title: When Appearances Deceive: A Silent Somatotroph Macroadenoma Presenting With Acromegaloid Features and Paradoxically Low Insulin-Like Growth Factor-1.
abstract: Silent somatotroph adenomas are uncommon pituitary neuroendocrine tumours (PitNETs) of the PIT1 lineage that express growth hormone (GH) immunohistochemically but without biochemical evidence of acromegaly. We report the case of a 32-year-old male patient referred with recurrent epistaxis, headache, right-sided diplopia, and third cranial nerve palsy. Clinical examination revealed acromegaloid features including frontal bossing, spade-like hands, and coarse facies, which were strongly suggestive of longstanding GH excess. However, preoperative insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) was paradoxically low at 13.1 nmol/L (reference range 15.5-33.1 nmol/L), creating a striking clinical-biochemical discordance. MRI demonstrated a giant sellar and suprasellar mass with chiasmal compression, right cavernous sinus invasion, and extension into the paranasal sinuses. The patient underwent endoscopic transsphenoidal resection. Neuropathology confirmed a densely granulated PIT1-lineage somatotroph adenoma with scattered GH positivity, diffuse Pit-1 staining, and a Ki-67 index below 2%. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge posed by silent somatotroph adenomas, underscores the limitations of biochemical assessment alone, and reinforces the essential role of histopathology and immunohistochemistry in establishing a definitive diagnosis. Long-term endocrine and neurosurgical surveillance is strongly recommended given the potential for phenotypic transformation to a functioning acromegaly syndrome.

title: EndoVLA-OOV: Language-Conditioned Out-of-View Target Acquisition in Robotic Endoscopy
abstract: The scan-then-revisit workflow of upper gastrointestinal endoscopy requires bringing a previously observed suspicious region back into view for closer inspection. Acquiring such targets requires translating anatomical and appearance descriptions into camera motions from partial observations of a confined, deformable environment. We present EndoVLA-OOV, a language-conditioned vision-language-action policy for out-of-view target acquisition in robotic endoscopy. The policy adapts a pretrained backbone to continuous two-degree-of-freedom distal bending commands and combines initial, intermediate, and current images to guide search. To support policy learning, we provide an open-source VLA dataset containing 1,050 episodes across six tasks and approximately 262k observation-action pairs. Physical evaluation spans wet-lens and low-light conditions, two unseen stomach phantoms, and cross-embodiment transfer to an unseen ex-vivo environment. In the cross-embodiment evaluation, the full-data policy achieves 93.3% target acquisition success (28/30). In a controlled training-data comparison, expanding the corpus from 312 to 1,050 episodes increases acquisition success from 40.0% to 90.0% under the same model, training, and test configuration. Instruction and observation interventions further support the use of language and temporal context in the evaluated acquisition tasks. These results support language-guided endoscopic revisitation across the evaluated environments and robot embodiments and demonstrate the benefit of expanded task-specific demonstrations.

title: Arbitrary-Scale Anisotropic 3D MRI Super-Resolution with Gaussian Prototypes
abstract: Reducing MRI acquisition time improves patient comfort, reduces motion artefacts, and increases scanner throughput. Clinical protocols often shorten acquisitions by sacrificing spatial resolution, particularly along the slice axis. Super-resolution can recover higher-resolution images, but existing methods are typically specialised to one scale or acquisition geometry, limiting their use across heterogeneous clinical protocols. We present GSMR3D, a continuous volumetric model that reconstructs arbitrary isotropic and anisotropic resolutions with a single checkpoint per MRI contrast. It combines a learned dictionary of anisotropic 3D Gaussian prototypes with scale-conditioned frequency encoding and an exact measurement-consistency projection, keeping reconstructions consistent with the acquired low-resolution data. We train separate models on 3,731 contrast-enhanced T1-weighted and 30,254 T1-weighted brain MRI volumes from clinical and population-based cohorts. We evaluate GSMR3D against geometry-specific specialists for isotropic, in-plane, and through-plane super-resolution using reconstruction quality and downstream tasks: brain tumour segmentation, brain-metastasis detection, and brain parcellation. GSMR3D outperforms specialists at isotropic $2\times$ and achieves better LPIPS, DISTS, and FID across all geometries, although specialists retain higher PSNR in anisotropic settings. It more faithfully preserves glioma segmentations across all geometries, achieves the highest lesion sensitivity on an independent brain-metastasis cohort, and the highest brain-parcellation agreement for isotropic and in-plane reconstruction. Reconstruction takes about 6s per volume, adding little overhead relative to acquisition-time savings. GSMR3D offers a flexible approach to MRI scan-time reduction with one model per contrast across geometries while preserving information relevant to downstream tasks.

title: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring
abstract: The adoption of Large Language Models for radiology report structuring has been largely dominated by either proprietary cloud-based models or large open models requiring high-end GPUs for deployment, which is a critical bottleneck for clinical adoption in radiology workflows that demand data privacy and offline operation. To address this, we present MedPAO-Assist, an edge-deployable agentic framework that generates structured radiology reports directly from radiologist dictation and voice commands, requiring only $\approx3.3$ GB peak RAM and achieving an average end-to-end latency of $\approx31$ seconds on a standard laptop CPU through an asynchronous, multi-threaded execution pipeline. The system currently supports four major imaging modalities -- Chest X-ray, Chest CT, Abdomen CT, and Brain MRI. To our knowledge, it is among the earliest agentic systems to run its entire pipeline with a Small Language Model (SLM) in the 0.6B-parameter range. This multi-agent architecture, built around an Extract-Ground-Generate paradigm, performs concept extraction, SNOMED-CT grounding, and structured report generation, followed by a speech-driven human-in-the-loop correction phase, together forming a fully "no-touch" reporting workflow that requires no keyboard input, external API calls, or internet connectivity. We evaluate each pipeline stage individually -- concept extraction, ontology grounding, and concept categorization and report hardware profiling results demonstrating the system's feasibility for real-time, CPU-only clinical deployment.
